We’ve sat on every side of this: founders selling into enterprises, operators transforming one from the inside, and executives responsible for enterprise AI. Marker is the company we wish we could have hired at Gap.

name: Kimpton
all_locations: New York City, NY, USA; Remote
long_description:
In investment management, every decision gets graded. The market prints the answer on a date known in advance, and nobody gets to argue with it.

Kimpton is financial AI that answers to reality. Kimpton OS is the AI-native operating system for investment teams: it does the research and hands PMs structured trades. EarningsBench is a public benchmark where models forecast quarterly earnings before companies report and the reported numbers do the scoring. Koliseum is the set of point-in-time financial environments we build from that work, for labs to train and evaluate models on.

The whole industry is fighting underperformance. Active managers trail their benchmarks, and capital keeps bleeding into passive. AI was supposed to fix that, but it hasn't. Funds either stitch together a dozen point tools or babysit general agents all day, and neither gets them to the trade.

Kimpton OS goes straight to it. It ingests a fund's mandate, strategy, and positions, connects to the institutional data the fund already runs on, and returns a structured trade proposal built for that fund. It's built to disagree, because consensus is poison for investment decisions. Instead of telling a PM what they want to hear, it surfaces the breaches and risks they'd otherwise miss.

That same work is how we grade AI. Static benchmarks leak into training data. Simulations reward what their authors imagined. A forecast sealed before the outcome exists and scored when the company reports can't be rehearsed or backdated. We started in markets because they're the one place reality answers on schedule.

We're two ex-Goldman engineers and an ex-SpaceX engineer. We left to start our own quantitative systematic hedge fund, raised $10M from a family office at 21 and 22, and scaled it to $35M over four years. We learned to trust live results over historical fit. We built Kimpton inside that fund, then productized the stack.

We're live with our first institutional client, a $3.3B manager. Our first market is fundamental equity funds from $1B to $10B, and the labs that need to know whether their models can do this work.

launches.title: Koliseum by Kimpton, Live Evaluation Arenas for AI Models
launches.tagline: Real-world market interaction environments, starting with financial markets
launches.body:
Today we're launching **Koliseum** by [Kimpton](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31420), live evaluation arenas for AI models in financial work.

**The problem**

Static benchmarks are contaminated soon after publication, and simulations reward the assumptions their designers encode. 

This simply isn't acceptable in finance or any other professional industry. A wrong answer or action can be catastrophic and reality eventually shows whether the claim was right. Almost no evaluation waits to find out.

**Koliseum**

Before Kimpton, we ran a quantitative fund. Backtests never proved alpha; live markets did. Koliseum applies the same test to models: a model commits inside an arena, the record is sealed, and reality supplies the grade.

Two kinds of arenas:

* **Prediction Arenas** seal a forecast before the outcome exists and score it against consensus, market, and statistical baselines when reality resolves.
* **Action Arenas** give a model a bounded task and real tools, then verify success from the resulting system state.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=113565&key=user_uploads/3054189/789d031b-cca8-4596-8921-dbc9f1544cb4)

The first Prediction Arena is already running. **EarningsBench** seals earnings forecasts for public companies 24 hours before each release and scores them against consensus and a statistical baseline once results are public.

Two things are already clear: most open-weight models reproduce consensus exactly, and a simple statistical baseline is harder to beat than a leaderboard alone would suggest.

Along with these developments, we are introducing a new concept in evaluation: **reality-as-a-judge**.

![uploaded image](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=113565&key=user_uploads%2F3054189%2Fc6c1ba2c-4e77-4ebc-be71-675f0abd71a6&variant=large)

Most open-ended evaluations are graded by another model or by a human rubric, so the score inherits the grader's assumptions. In reality-as-a-judge, the grader is the outcome itself.

[More info on Koliseum](https://www.kimpton.ai/koliseum)

[Methodology](https://www.kimpton.ai/methodology)

**Our ask**

Reach out if:

* You work on post-training or evals at a lab and want your model in the first private cohort. Results stay private unless you publish them.
* You run a trading firm or a prediction venue and want models scored on your own resolving questions, or want to co-run a public arena.
* You have a workflow (any industry!) with a verifiable end state and want it turned into an Action Arena.

or know anyone who does.

Write to us at [founders@kimpton.ai](mailto:founders@kimpton.ai). Thanks for the support!

launches.title: Kimpton: Cursor for portfolio managers
launches.tagline: AI-native terminal where agents do the research and propose the trades
launches.body:
**TL;DR** AI can’t trade, but portfolio managers can. Kimpton combines high-resolution public financial markets data, portfolio manager strategy/mandate, portfolio holdings, and transaction data to generate trade ideas for managers.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3aED4nL3G50>

**Our Background**

We are former Goldman Sachs and Vistra Energy engineers who started a quantitative hedge fund together in 2021 after raising $10M from a family office at the ages of 22 and 21 years old, scaling it to $35M at its peak.

We spent four years systematically trading using the tools that we built in-house to support our systems. Internally, we developed Kimpton to automate many of our own workflows.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102078&key=user_uploads/3054189/7f252d74-65d7-4557-92f0-59383e3a782a)

**The Problem**

AI can’t trade. After all, LLMs are the most overfit backtest in all of human history. They are consensus machines and sycophantic by nature. As a result, AI goes largely unused by portfolio managers today.

Agents finally had depth in 2025. We tested LLMs on the markets and were unimpressed with the output. LLMs can’t trade because they are consensus machines and sycophantic by nature. They lack the edge that portfolio managers provide.

AI can’t trade like a portfolio manager, but they can research at 100X the efficiency of an investment analyst. For this reason, Kimpton revolves around the portfolio manager, solving increasingly all of the workflows that they need.

Analysts spend weeks aggregating data and synthesizing it to generate singular trade ideas that are passed up to portfolio managers for review. It’s time for a change.

Investment management is built on the idea that analysts and PMs need to spend their days staring at screens all day to find edge in the markets. 

To refactor the investment management industry, we can’t simply provide better tools. We have to automate the entire research layer instead.

**The Solution**

Kimpton automates the analysis layer by securely ingesting firm-wide context, portfolio, and transaction data to synthesize fully-formed trade recommendations fitted to their portfolio.

Portfolio managers can challenge the results of the trade proposals through a process we call Adversarial Review, an agentic Socratic questioning to assist portfolio managers in coming to their own conclusions.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102078&key=user_uploads/3054189/62ecf56b-91f8-4c4d-a883-6a8be7df6108)

We developed a harness specifically for the financial markets to make aggregation efficient, fast, and accurate. It has access to high-quality institutional data sources through Factset, Massive, and Tiingo. Real-time data on tens of thousands of global assets across equities, ETFs, indices, insider trades, SEC filings, events, transcripts, company fundamentals, corporate leadership, and more!

Our AI agents also provide portfolio managers with the ability to generate many different types of artifacts, such as real-time dashboards, institutional-grade reports, and comprehensive visualizations.

**Traction**

Kimpton is deployed and generating trade proposals on billions of dollars of assets under management today.

Portfolio managers are using Kimpton to monitor their exposures, understand investment thesis drift, earnings coverage, manage positioning across teams, investor reporting, and as an investment team collective brain.

Portfolio managers are underserved today when the potential to refactor the way they work is massive. Kimpton is focused on improving the lives portfolio managers who are actively making decisions in the public markets.

**Ask**

If you know anyone who manages assets a hedge fund, family office, mutual fund, ETF manager, or other public markets manager — we’d love to speak with them.

Enterprise software takes months to go live after the sale. Imagine paying for an app on the app store but not being able to use it for 6 months. [Lab0](https://lab0.ai/) solves exactly this.

We’re building an AI FDE that automates entire post-sales delivery for software companies - all from discovery, solution design, config, to testing and go-live. We’re currently working with Adobe and a couple of system integrators.

The future of enterprise software is self-serve, where enterprises buy a product, and it gets configured by agents.

[Lab0](https://www.linkedin.com/company/lab0-hq/) is the AI FDE making that real: 6 months → 10 days.

<https://youtu.be/UDrqfnYWlLI>

# **The problem**

If you've sold to an enterprise, you know this already.

A $200K contract lands. Hand off to post-sales. On a deeper technical discovery of your client’s processes, you realize you need a lot of custom changes to serve them.

That's the hidden tax on every enterprise sale, 3 months of bespoke FDE / Solution Architect’s work, rebuilt from scratch for every customer. That’s 3 months of lost value for the customer.

Either you wait months to start billing, or somehow show enough ROI in the remaining duration of the contract to get a renewal.

# **What we built**

[Lab0](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/lab0) is the AI FDE for your (AI?) B2B SaaS. It joins discovery calls and tells you what to ask, generates handoffs, design documents and test plans. It even configures the product, writes custom integrations and tests all the workflows before signing off.

_Six months of services work, done in days._

launches.body:
**Hey everyone 👋**

I'm Justin, founder of Sidekick.

**TL;DR** Sidekick is an AI assistant that frontline manufacturing workers use over text message. They text a number and it answers from the company's own documents, creates and routes work orders, and syncs with the software the company already uses. No app, no login, no training. I built Sidekick for my dad's manufacturing shop. It’s now live at facilities across the globe.

**_Ask:_** Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility? I'd love an intro! Email [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick).

Check out our launch video:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yxwq5ZAojXg>

## ❌ The Problem

I grew up in my dad's manufacturing plants and spent summers working on the factory floor at EDS Manufacturing.

Here's what I watched happen repeatedly. A machine goes down, everyone's waiting, and the person who can help is in a meeting or on another line. Half the time the answer already existed. Nobody could get to it.

Why it keeps happening:

* **No computer access.** Nobody on that floor has a company login or an email address, so none of the plant's software reaches them.
* **The answers are scattered.** An SOP in a binder, a manual on a shared drive few have permissions to, a safety procedure someone printed and taped to a wall in 2019.
* **The best answers were never written down.** Thirty years of tribal knowledge lives in one guy's head, and when he retires it leaves with him.
* **So the same questions get asked over and over.** Shift after shift, and every one of them costs somebody their afternoon.

There are 239,000 manufacturing plants in the US, and only 29% of the people working in them have advanced digital skills. Any tool that requires a download, a login, and training makes adoption difficult.

## ✅ Our Solution

Workers text the Sidekick phone number. Problems, photos, voice memos, in any language. No app to download, no account to create, nothing to learn. Every worker on the floor already knows how to send a text, which is why adoption isn't a fight.

* **Answers from your own documents.** SOPs, manuals, safety procedures, tribal knowledge. Sidekick responds in the worker's language, in seconds.
* **Creates and routes the work order.** The issue gets logged and sent to the right person, without anyone needing a laptop.
* **Syncs with the software you already run.** Sidekick pulls from and writes to your existing systems instead of replacing them, and integrates directly through PLC and SCADA systems so the floor and the software finally see the same thing.
* **Captures tribal knowledge.** Every exchange builds a searchable knowledge base the company owns, so the know-how stays when the veteran leaves.

Here's a full walkthrough:

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a5zBRSXi-90>

## 👤 The Team

I'm Justin, founder and CEO. I'm the third generation in a manufacturing family, and I've been around plant floors since I was a kid. I studied Computer Science at the University of Pennsylvania, worked in finance at Arm, and left both to build Sidekick after watching the same problem play out on every floor I'd been on.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If you answer "yes" to any of these, I'd love your help:

* **Do you know anyone who owns or runs a manufacturing plant, warehouse, or industrial facility?** Even a name and a "you two should talk" goes a long way.
* **Have you sold software into manufacturing?** I'd love to hear what actually worked and what didn't.

Contact me at [**justin@textsidekick.com**](mailto:justin@textsidekick.com) or [**book a demo here**](https://calendly.com/justin-textsidekick)**.**

launches.body:
### **⚡TL;DR**

**Infera is the Claude Code for scientific instruments.** Describe an experiment in plain English, and Infera turns it into a validated, instrument-ready run, handling the protocol logic, vendor scripts, data, and inventory across the instruments your lab already uses. One system, from intent to execution.

### 🤔 **The Problem**

Labs run on hardware from the future and software from the past.

The instruments are extraordinary. Mass specs identify thousands of proteins, flow cytometers read tens of thousands of cells a second, and cryo-EMs image at near-atomic resolution. These are the machines behind biomarker discovery, immunotherapy, structural biology, and drug development. But the software around them still looks like it shipped in 2003, and runs like it.

We've watched labs running \~6 instruments from 3+ vendors write a one-off script for every experiment, stitch outputs together by hand, and track inventory in a Google Sheet someone probably forgot to update last Tuesday. Scientists spend their week being human glue between machines that should already talk to each other.

### **🔍How Infera Works**

[**Demo Video**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3GPze4X7AeA)

**I. Describe the experiment in plain English.** Infera asks the right questions, surfaces edge cases, and checks against your lab’s inventory and instrument state.

**II. Infera turns it into a run, accommodating both manual and automatable steps.** For programmable instruments, it generates vendor-specific scripts, executes, pulls the data back, and runs the analysis. For manual work like pipetting, gels, hand fermentation, etc., it's the context layer underneath: which step you're on, which reagent goes where, what could go wrong, and how others in the lab have run it before.

**III. The knowledge stays.** Every protocol, every validated run, every edge case becomes part of the system and checked against instrument constraints, lab SOPs, inventory, and prior experiments.

That last part is the hard part. It's what general-purpose LLMs can't do, and it's what enables a researcher to trust the output the way they'd trust a trained technician.

### 👩‍🔬 **Team**

Hi! We’re Chloe and Troy, and we're building Infera to close the gap between science and instrumentation.

* Chloe studied Mechanical Engineering at Harvard. She's been building research software and medical devices since before college (Regeneron STS Scholar), including a microfluidic device that detects harmful chemicals in household products, and has been doing research at places like Fred Hutch, Brigham and Women's, Harvard Medical School, and Pacific Northwest National Lab.
* Troy studied Computation & Neural Systems at Caltech, where he held an endowed research fellowship in a top research lab as an undergraduate. He's published two first-author cancer papers, holds a first-inventor agtech patent, and built and sold two companies before Infera.

Between us, we've run experiments by hand, written the scripts, and watched the whole system break when one person leaves. That's the problem we're building Infera to fix.

### **🎯Ask**

We're currently running pilots with Boston-area academic labs and cores. If any of these are you, reach out at [**hello@infera.bio**](mailto:hello@infera.bio):

* **Academic labs and cores:** know a PI or core director in proteomics, genomics, flow, automation, or screening? We'd love an intro, and we're happy to set up a pilot
* **YC founders with wet labs (diagnostics, therapeutics, synbio, tools):** we’d love to meet whoever runs your lab ops
* **Biotech and life sciences folks:** come say hi
* **Instrument manufacturers** whose customers wish the software were better, let's talk

launches.title: Expanse - Unlock wasted GPU capacity
launches.tagline: Unlock wasted GPU capacity.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Expanse unlocks wasted GPU capacity. We’re the intelligence layer for compute infrastructure. Submit jobs with the right resources. Optimise them to run faster. Debug failures in seconds, not days. Works on cloud and on-prem HPC.

Want to know how much more you can get out of your hardware? Schedule a call: <https://book.getexpanse.io>

**Problem**

Running compute on a cluster means guessing memory, time, and GPUs before you submit. Get it wrong and your job fails mid-run. Over-guess and you pay for compute you never use. 30% of cloud spend is lost to over-allocation \[1\]. Microsoft Research found their own deep learning jobs hit 50% GPU utilisation or lower \[2\].

Sizing jobs takes decades of experience. Memory patterns, batching, GPU threading, CPU vectorisation. AI agents don’t have enough information to fix it either. SLURM and Kubernetes don’t expose enough structured data. Even strong platform teams are forced to choose: spend time debugging and optimising every job, or accept the waste. AI infrastructure spending will hit $2.52 trillion in 2026 \[3\]. The waste grows with every new cluster. This problem isn’t going away.

**Solution**

Expanse learns your cluster. We analyse your code and hardware telemetry, then track them over time. Our deep learning models build a picture of what your workloads actually need. Predictions get sharper with every job.

Our models are deployed on your cluster. All analysis runs on your network. Your code and telemetry never leave your infrastructure. We can’t see your data, and you maintain full data sovereignty.

One command installs Expanse on your cluster. You get two tools.

`expanse analyse` - for every job:

* **Suggests the right resource configuration**
* **Predicts failures from historical code and telemetry patterns**
* **Surfaces code-level optimisations that increase efficiency**

`expanse diagnose` - for every failure:

* **Finds the root cause**
* **Returns solution-oriented logs with the exact code and config changes to fix it**

Days of debugging and optimising become seconds. Platform teams get what they need to do this in minutes instead of weeks.

**Founders**

We're four engineers from the University of Edinburgh, all coming from top quant funds and national supercomputing centres. Ismaeel built the first multimodal HPC resource predictor at EPCC (Edinburgh's Parallel Computing Centre), beating every published baseline. Yafet built the first GNN cluster graph network for predicting SLURM queue wait times. Eren built decentralised foundation model training systems at Edinburgh. Niko trained large-scale speech ML models on GPU clusters and architected cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure at one of the largest hedge funds in the world. We left our jobs to fix this ourselves.

**CTA / Ask**

Running compute and not getting enough out of what you’re paying for? Failing jobs, unclear errors, bills too high? We’d love to chat.

Know anyone in AI infrastructure (managing cloud and/or on-premise data centres), quant finance, drug discovery, or AI research labs? An intro would mean a lot :)

**YC Deal**

All YC companies running serious ML training can contact us for a discounted pilot. We’ll find inefficiencies and wastage on your compute setup. Then we deploy Expanse, no changes to your workflows. You get more out of the hardware you’re paying for.

Reach out: [founders@expanse.sh](mailto:founders@expanse.sh) or <https://book.getexpanse.io>

References

\[1\] <https://grafana.com/blog/2023/03/03/how-to-optimize-resource-utilization-with-kubernetes-monitoring-for-grafana-cloud>

\[2\] <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/an-empirical-study-on-low-gpu-utilization-of-deep-learning-jobs/>

\[3\] <https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-1-15-gartner-says-worldwide-ai-spending-will-total-2-point-5-trillion-dollars-in-2026>

launches.body:
Hey YC 👋\
\
We’re Rayan and Maadhav, and today we’re excited to launch [Enjamb Labs](https://www.enjamb.ai/).

<https://youtu.be/5DwdtiLvViM>\
\
**TL;DR**

Enjamb runs the entire drug program for biopharma teams, from discovery to FDA approval. \
\
Pharma runs on decades of closed legacy systems like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS, with no AI layer and no MCP to connect agents to them. So we built that connection layer. \
\
Our agents run on top of their existing systems and data, with no migration, and do the work across the whole program: clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.\
\
In just 3 weeks since launch, we're already being used by 500+ employees at top pharma companies, including Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merck & Sanofi.

**The Problem: Pharma’s systems have no AI layer**

It costs $2.6 billion and 10+ years to ship a single drug, and most of that isn't the science. It's the work around it, spread across decades of closed legacy systems that don't talk to each other:

* Benchling stores the data
* Veeva holds the documents
* Medidata runs the trials
* SAS does the stats

Agents are **_finally_**  good enough to do real scientific work. But there's no AI layer on these systems, and no MCP to plug an agent into where pharma's data and work actually live.

**So, we built that connection layer we wished existed.**\
\
**What We Offer: Agents that run on top of pharma’s existing systems**

Enjamb invented the fastest way to run a drug program: a single agentic workspace that unifies the evidence, analysis, and regulatory work.

Our agents:

* Synthesize up-to-date clinical evidence from the literature and real-world data to pinpoint the right endpoints and patient populations
* Design trials and run the statistical programming behind them, including SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, and QC
* Draft and audit regulatory documents like INDs, protocols, SAPs, and NDAs

— all in one auditable workspace, with the context carried end to end.\
\
**The results:** Enjamb generates an FDA submission package in **48 hours** instead of 8 months, with **23x fewer errors** than GPT-5.5. And **98%** of the datasets it produces pass Pinnacle 21, the FDA's standard, on the first pass, before a human even reviews.\
\
**And it all runs in the browser**: full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint editors, a Python and R compute environment, 100+ scientific integrations, and 50+ fine-tuned models for in-silico validation. No setup.

\
**Our Story: Two Researchers Who Lived the Problem**

We're **Rayan** (ML/Bio researcher, first-author paper @ JMIR, presented @ SOT and ISCB, beat SOTA by 20%) and **Maadhav** (ex-Dell AI Lab, ex-Broadcom R&D).\
\
We kept hitting the same wall in research: the science was the easy part. Everything around it, the evidence, the analysis, the documents, was fragmented, manual, and disconnected, and the context died at every handoff.\
\
So we built what we always wanted: one workspace where agents carry the context across the entire drug program.

**If no one's going to build it right, we will.**\
\
**Get Started**

* See Enjamb at [enjamb.ai](http://enjamb.ai)
* Or reach us at [rayan@enjamb.ai](mailto:rayan@enjamb.ai) for a demo

launches.title: Agentmuxer by Amorphic Labs - OpenRouter for Agent Capabilities
launches.tagline: One MCP and one wallet for agents to find, pay for, and use the best tools for any task
launches.body:
**tl;dr: OpenRouter became the router for model spend; we're building that layer for agent capabilities, starting with paid tools: web search, scraping, extraction, enrichment, and more from top providers in each category. No provider accounts or API keys, one balance, pay per use. We benchmark every provider on real tasks and route each request to the one that performs best, with fallbacks when a provider fails. We're looking for early users to try it out with free credits, email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com) if you want to check it out!**

**Launch Video:**

<https://youtu.be/-dxc8ZAUfFc>

**The problem:**

Agents can only use the tools a human wired up in advance, and they won't tell you what they're missing: they quietly make do, failing at anything they weren't hand-equipped for. Even when you do the wiring, you're picking blind: nobody actually knows which search API is better for this query, or which scraper will survive this site. The "best setup" frontier moves daily, so keeping up means hours of trawling MCP directories, X threads, and blog posts. Agents stay only as capable as their setup, and the more autonomous they get, the more that ceiling costs.

**What we do:**

Your agent asks for what it needs ("structured data from this page", "research this with citations"). We route the request to the best provider for that specific task, based on benchmarks on real tasks and outcome feedback from the agents using them: success rates, result quality, latency, and cost. If a provider fails, we cascade to the next, so your agent gets a result instead of an error. Every request makes the routing smarter. One balance pays for all of it, and it's the same MCP whether it's your own coding agent or agents you're shipping in a product.

APIs are just the start. The same marketplace will let agents acquire skills, hire other agents for specialized tasks, and sign up for software directly through MCPs, all from one balance.

**Our team:**

We're Frank and Dylan, friends of 10 years who have been building together since middle school. Frank was a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI and interned at Two Sigma, NVIDIA, and Amazon. Dylan was a quant trading intern at UBS, co-authored a NeurIPS paper, and was a grand finalist and 8th-best speaker in the world at WSDC 2022. We built this because we kept hitting the problem ourselves: agents stuck mid-task waiting for us to make accounts and guess at providers.

**Our ask:**

1. Want to be an early user? Email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com) and we'll onboard you with free credits.
2. If you sell an API, dataset, or agent-facing service and want agents as customers, we'd love to talk about listing you. Email us at [founders@amorphiclabs.com](mailto:founders@amorphiclabs.com)
3. If you want more information or want to join the waitlist, check out [agentmuxer.com](http://agentmuxer.com)

_Make something agents want!_

launches.title: Amorphic Labs - Agentic, Personalized Product Demo Videos for Sales
launches.tagline: AI agents that create personalized demos at scale for outbound, inbound, and call follow-ups without your team recording a thing.
launches.body:
**tl;dr: We build AI agents that create personalized product demo videos for outbound, inbound qualification, and post-call follow-ups. Just give us a demo account for your app and a list of prospects, and our agent researches each prospect, uses its own computer to record a tailored workflow in your app with seeded personalized data, then edits and narrates the video so it is ready to send as a link to each prospect.**

**Launch Video:**

<https://youtu.be/uq9LyHYYyOU>

**Our Ask:**

* If you’re a founder or part of a startup that sells software, we can help you give every prospect a tailored product experience while saving your team hours of recording time. Book a demo at [amorphiclabs.com](http://amorphiclabs.com)!
* If you know any sales or RevOps leaders, we would love introductions or referrals to them.

**The Problem:**

Recording a personalized product demo is one of the clearest ways to communicate your value and show someone how your product solves their problems, but preparing a demo environment, seeding data, and recording a high-quality video for every prospect takes too long. As a result, teams skip personalized demos in situations where they could be highly effective, such as outbound, and spend hours every week creating them for inbound requests and post-call follow-ups. This means teams miss opportunities to show prospects exactly how their product fits their needs, while wasting hours that could have been spent talking to and selling to prospects.

**The Solution:**

We use AI agents to create personalized product demo videos at scale, bringing tailored demos to parts of the sales process where they were previously too time-consuming to produce. All you need to provide is a demo account for your app and a list of prospects.

Our agent then:

* Learns and interacts with your app on its own computer like a real sales engineer.
* Researches each prospect to determine which workflow and data best fit their needs.
* Seeds personalized data in your app.
* Records itself completing the relevant workflow.
* Edits the video to remove long waits and adds effects such as zooms.
* Narrates the video with a script tailored to the prospect.
* Gives you a finished video link ready to send.

You remain fully in control of how the videos are created: you can clone your own voice, define the workflows the agent can choose from, control the narration style and how each video begins and ends, and regenerate videos by giving the agent feedback.

**Sample video our agent generated:**

<https://youtu.be/QONd3u3NoGo>

**Where you can use it:**

Tailored Outbound: You can import a list of leads you want to reach out to and ask our agent to create personalized demos for each one, showing prospects exactly how your product fits their needs through data, workflows, and narration tailored directly to them.

Qualifying Inbound: Add a request-a-demo form to your landing page so prospects who are not yet convinced enough to spend 30 minutes on a discovery call can spend 20 seconds requesting a personalized demo video and receive an email showing exactly how your product solves their problems.

Call Follow-ups: After understanding a prospect’s key use cases and pain points during a discovery call, you can create multiple personalized demo videos showing how you address their needs. You can even create additional videos tailored to different stakeholders that your champion can use to sell your product internally.

We are initially focused on sales, but the same technology can also create walkthrough videos for onboarding, customer support, and documentation.

**Our team:**

We have been best friends for close to a decade, have competed together in competitions spanning math, debate, pitching, business, and hackathons, built countless projects, and are now building Amorphic Labs together.

Frank worked as a software engineer for three years while graduating from UW. He was a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI and previously interned at Two Sigma, NVIDIA, and Amazon.

Dylan was a quantitative trading intern at UBS and recently graduated from Georgia Tech. He represented Team China twice at WSDC, was a grand finalist and the eighth-best speaker in the world in 2022, and co-authored a paper published at NeurIPS.

**If you sell software and want to see what our agent could create for one of your prospects, book a demo at [amorphiclabs.com](http://amorphiclabs.com).**

launches.title: GitCafe: A Git forge for teams and agents shipping hundreds of times a day, not twice.
launches.tagline: The Git forge for agent-scale teams
launches.body:
Software development is becoming much more parallel. Coding agents let a team have dozens or hundreds of related changes moving at the same time, creating more branches, reviews, CI runs, and automation than existing workflows were designed to absorb.

Today, we’re opening GitCafe in public beta. It is a Git forge built for teams where humans and coding agents may ship hundreds or thousands of changes a day. We’re building the hosting, review, CI, security, and automation layer for that way of working.\
\
Hundreds of users are already on GitCafe, and we’re currently running trials with roughly a dozen YC companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109445&key=user_uploads/1920545/eecbfb4f-82f1-4660-8ee8-aeea5273a8b9)

Generating code is only part of the problem. Teams still need to understand what is changing, review it safely, keep CI moving, catch security issues, and coordinate work without becoming overwhelmed.

We’re not building GitCafe because putting repositories, code review, and CI in one product is new. We’re building it because we believe the workload those systems need to support is about to change dramatically.

We started by rebuilding the Git infrastructure itself. Now we’re closing the product gap feature by feature.

Recently, we added secret scanning, Buildkite and Harmont CI support, stacked diffs with Jujutsu and Sapling integration, and beta support for GitHub Actions.

These are foundational capabilities, not the destination. Building them on infrastructure we own gives us a base we can keep extending for higher-volume, agent driven development.

The honest version is that GitCafe is behind GitHub today. GitHub has spent more than a decade building an enormous product, and GitCafe does not yet have every workflow, administrative control, or integration that mature teams need. Some features are missing, some are experimental, and some edges are rough. We expect to earn the broader product surface, not claim it on day one.

We’re opening GitCafe now because the fastest way to improve it is to put it in the hands of teams doing real work.

If your team is already using coding agents heavily, try GitCafe at <https://git.cafe> and tell us where the workflow breaks down.\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=blHKFEOmoFg>

launches.title: Kebra — Making the field queryable
launches.tagline: We capture what happens in field operations and turn it into the context AI employees need to automate the work that follows
launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋

We’re [Luca](https://www.linkedin.com/in/luca-hadife/) and [Hosny](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohamed-hosny-hussein/), founders of [Kebra](https://kebra.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=yc_launch_2026).

## TL;DR

Kebra makes the field queryable.

We capture what happens across jobs, sites, and assets and turn it into a live operating memory that AI can query and act on. Our AI employees use that context to automate the work that follows across the systems companies already use.

Every job makes that memory richer, building the company specific context software agents use today and physical agents will need tomorrow.

We’re already working with field operations companies across Florida, Pennsylvania, and California.

<https://youtu.be/VIwv5iVm8Ok>

## The problem

Field operations never got their Claude Code moment.

We spent months inside HVAC companies trying to automate their back office. We built AI employees for claims, reporting, coordination, and follow ups.

They kept breaking.

Not because the AI could not do the work, but because it was acting on a reality that never happened. The most important part of the operation happened on the ground and was never properly captured.

A missing serial number. A photo never taken. What the technician actually found stuck in their head.

You cannot automate an alternate reality. Before AI can operate the field, the field has to become queryable.

## Our Solution

Kebra makes field operations queryable.

**Capture what happens:** Field teams document jobs through photos, voice, video, and structured workflows. Kebra checks what is missing while they are still on site.

**Build the operating memory:** Every job updates a live history of sites, assets, repairs, decisions, and how the company actually works.

**AI employees act on it:** They use that context to automate reports, claims, coordination, compliance, follow ups, and other back office work across the systems the company already uses.

## Vision

Every job makes Kebra’s operating memory richer.

Today, software agents use that context to automate field operations. Tomorrow, physical AI and robots will need the same company specific context to understand each site, asset, procedure, and history before they can work autonomously.

Kebra is building the context layer for field operations.

## Our Ask

Run or know a company with field operations where important information gets lost between the field and the office?

Email us at [founders@kebra.com](mailto:founders@kebra.com) and [book a demo](https://calendar.app.google/s1DwDxHTbxZ9w5Uq6).\
Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/kebra-com)

name: HERA
long_description: At Hera, we build tools that help heavy engineering teams bring products to market up to 20× faster. Today, we work with manufacturers of data center ancillary equipment, renewable energy systems, robotics, heat exchangers, power plants and pressure vessels.
one_liner: We make sure every factory in the world builds without mistakes.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
American manufacturers lose an estimated $285,000 annually to poor quality for every $10 million in revenue. At the same time, the industry is losing the engineers who know how to prevent those losses. Nearly 4 million manufacturing jobs will need to be filled by 2033 as experienced workers retire, and almost half are expected to go unfilled. Much of the expertise required to review complex engineering drawings exists only in the heads of senior engineers who are leaving the workforce.

We're both engineers who grew up watching this firsthand. After more than 200 conversations with manufacturing engineers, quality engineers and machinists, we're building software that captures that expertise by automatically reviewing engineering drawings against ASME standards and company-specific rules before they ever reach the shop floor.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
We're building the largest repository of engineering judgment in the world. We tailor each company's checks to their own standards, the kind usually mastered by only a handful of senior engineers. We turn that knowledge into software every plant can use the same week.

With success, the physical things the world depends on get built 10x faster, and a retiring generation's expertise is never lost.

launches.title: HERA: catches thousand-dollar drawing mistakes before the shop floor.
launches.tagline: Hera reviews every drawing against your factory's own standards and the ASME code, catching expensive mistakes and preventing rework 10x faster than manual review.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Every custom metal part starts as a drawing, and every drawing gets checked by hand before anyone builds it. Hera does that check in minutes instead of a full day, and catches the mistakes that turn into scrapped parts.**

[**https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y**](https://youtu.be/J_5NRjkou3Y)

**The Problem**

Custom mechanical parts run on 2D drawings. Whether you're an OEM releasing drawings to suppliers, or an aerospace supplier answering to source inspection, every drawing has to be checked against ASME/ISO standards and GD&T requirements before it goes anywhere near a machine.

Right now, that review is done by hand, and usually by the most senior engineer in the building. And a single missed tolerance callout or an ambiguous datum reference can mean a scrapped part, a blown schedule, or a shipment that fails inspection.

We heard the same story from a pressure vessel fabricator, a semiconductor tooling shop, and a medical device manufacturer: reviews take days. This isn't because the work is hard. There's simply no good way to do it faster without cutting corners, and nobody cuts corners on a drawing that could scrap a $40,000 part.

**Our Solution**

Hera is a brain for manufacturing. Any real advance in manufacturing has to be grounded in two things: the standards parts are held to and the reality of the shop floor. So that's what we built Hera on.

Upload a drawing and Hera checks GD&T callouts, tolerance stack ups, and title block requirements against ASME Y14.5, relevant ISO standards, and your own design intent. The result is a drawing your shop can build right the first time, without the delays and rework that eat margins. Every review also makes Hera more valuable, creating a system of record for drawing errors that helps teams build better models for engineering processes.

**While the current review takes days, Hera takes minutes… and gets better by the drawing.**

**Us**

**Noelle** grew up in an industrial park her family runs in the Philippines and has been on factory floors her whole life. At 19, she built a water-treatment facility that added 40 L/s of capacity to the park. 

**Meera** has spent years around manufacturing: at her family's plants, and on projects at Pfizer and TE Connectivity, where she built a SOTA discrete-event simulation. She taught herself PLC programming and C++, and has published ML research at UW.

We actually met on a bus to a factory tour, and have been best friends ever since!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107030&key=user_uploads/3352287/d05e9e1a-57c8-4e43-91d7-75e42a004261)

**Our Ask** If you run or work at a factory (aerospace, semiconductor, medical device, pressure vessel, or custom machinery), we want to visit you! If you invite us out to see your shop, we’ll come by in person and bring you a **customized Hera Swiss Army knife**.

Reach out to us at [**founders@manufacturingintelligence.org**](mailto:founders@manufacturingintelligence.org).

launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Peyton and Michael Marcotte, brothers and co-founders of [Perceptron ML (YC S26)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/perceptronml/). We make law firms AI-native: we build the AI and software a firm needs to scale. Not a product off the shelf, a system built around how your firm already works, where no fact is used until it traces to a real document.

[Perceptron ML (YC S26) Launch Video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1c-5RUaBQsJWG-6vJsy0O8PLvAcgpuEco/view)

**The problem.** In 2023, two New York lawyers filed a brief written by AI that cited six cases that did not exist. Courts have caught it more than a thousand times since. So most firms went back to doing everything by hand, and by hand the math is brutal: lawyers lose \~40% of their day to work that isn't law, and tens of billions in legal work goes unclaimed every year because firms can't move fast enough to take it.

**What we do.** Every firm's bottleneck is different, and it is never the one on the shelf. So we build what each firm actually needs: intake answered and filed at 2 a.m., demands drafted from the record, records requests chased until they land, deadlines and statutes watched, every hour matched to its matter, clients updated by text before they think to call. Every firm gets something different, but underneath it's all the same platform we built once: our grounding engine, our connectors into the firm's systems, and our agent runtime. That's what lets us build this broadly without being an agency.

**Why you can trust it.** The AI we build doesn't guess. Every fact traces to a real document, verified against the primary source before a model can use it. Click anything, and the original opens.

**Why us.** [Michael](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marcottemichael/) did AI research at NVIDIA (hardware-debugging agent in production). [Peyton](https://www.linkedin.com/in/peytonmarcotte/) led two NASA-supported research projects. We come from places where a confident wrong answer is unacceptable, and we started Perceptron ML because law is the biggest industry still run by hand for exactly that reason.

**The ask.** If you know a managing partner, or the attorney who signs your invoices, we'd love an intro: [founders@perceptronml.com](mailto:founders@perceptronml.com)

[perceptronml.com](http://perceptronml.com)

launches.title: Trope - Modernize ERP implementations with AI
launches.tagline: The AI-native platform to deliver successful ERP implementations faster.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! We're [Matthew](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mdchow/) and [Victor](https://www.linkedin.com/in/victor-vannara/) - cofounders of [Trope](https://trope.ai/). We’re building the AI-native platform for ERP services.

**TLDR**

* After buying an ERP, companies spend over $50B a year on consulting services to get the software implemented
* 70% of ERP implementations fail to meet budget, timelines, or targets
* Trope deploys agents to help ERP implementation teams deliver projects on time and on budget from one AI-native platform

**Launch Video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mhDiw0nKB34>

\
**❌ Problem**

Companies buy an ERP expecting it to become the most powerful software in their stack. It runs finance, inventory, procurement, operations, reporting, and the workflows the business depends on.

Buying an ERP is easy. Implementing it is hard and requires labour heavy consultant work where:

* Requirements get missed
* Workflows get configured differently than agreed
* Data issues get discovered too late
* Testing reveals the system does not match how the business actually works
* End-user adoption suffers

For implementation teams, the challenge is managing hundreds of stakeholders across concurrent projects, with thousands of documents, decisions, and system dependencies to track.

That is why so many ERP projects miss their budget, timeline, and targets, and why companies spend billions on implementation services.

**✅ Solution**

Trope is the AI-native platform that deploys agents to deliver successful implementations faster.

Using Trope is like having a project manager, consultant, and developer working 24/7, so you can spend more time on the design and decisions.

Trope connects to the systems where project work already lives. It compares what was promised with what is actually being built, then flags gaps across scope, configuration, data, testing, training, and documentation before they become expensive.

Trope takes action by turning meetings into action items, scanning ERP configurations programmatically, and keeping documents, configurations, and stakeholders in sync.

**The Team**

We grew up in Vancouver and met at the University of British Columbia. We built operations and AI software at Tesla, Amazon, Zipline, and Schneider Electric.

After speaking with ERP veterans who had built and sold practices, the pattern was clear: everyone knew the traditional services model was going to change, but no one knew how.

Trope is defining the AI-native model for ERP services.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104941&key=user_uploads/2519723/896d82bc-589c-4f7b-a0a7-59d2c9fc8d9f)

**Our Ask**

If you know anyone who works on ERP implementations (ie, consulting, system integration, or professional services) we’d love an intro. Email me at [matthew@trope.ai](mailto:matthew@trope.ai).

Take care,

Matthew & Victor

launches.title: Kara: Making Diamond an Engineering Material
launches.tagline: Kara grows and engineers diamond wafers for thermal management, semiconductor and quantum applications
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We grow high-purity diamond wafers for scientific and industrial applications. Our diamond thermal wafers can be used in aircraft, spacecraft, RF electronics, and lasers to move heat dramatically better than conventional materials. We’re helping hardware run cooler, faster, and more reliably with diamond that is 5× more thermally conductive than copper.

Here is a link to our launch video: 

<https://youtu.be/16aad1cU_FM>

**The Problem**

The world’s most valuable hardware systems are limited by how quickly they can remove heat.

For AI chips, that means expensive GPUs throttle and deliver less compute. In aircraft and satellites, it means carrying more cooling mass. In RF systems and lasers, it limits sustained output power.

Adding more cooling costs space, and energy, and sometimes is simply not possible.

**What We Built**

Diamond is usually something you wear. We make it something engineers can build with.

Diamond conducts heat up to **5× better than copper while weighing \~60% less** for the same volume. It is electrically insulating and stable in extreme environments.

Today we manufacture:

* Diamond heat spreaders for AI and high-performance computing
* Ultra-high-purity diamond wafers for thermal, photonic and quantum applications
* Diamond-metal composites (copper and aluminium) for thermal management
* Metallized and bondable diamond plates
* Custom-engineered diamond components

We are now producing custom samples under pilot agreements and purchase orders for thermal, electronic, aerospace, and quantum applications.

Silicon transformed computing when we learned to manufacture it with extreme purity and control. Kara is doing the same with diamond. Today, our ultra-high-purity diamond pulls heat away from silicon chips.

**Tomorrow, Kara’s control over purity and defects unlocks diamond as the ultimate semiconductor.**

**Why us**

[@Aarin Jhaveri](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669602) is a fifth-generation diamantaire who has sold millions of dollars in natural and lab-grown diamonds and worked across the supply chain.

[@Anuveer Chadha](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3669310) is a chemical engineer who has worked on diamond quantum sensing and advanced-materials research at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with the Department of Defense and Department of Energy.

Diamond is our unfair advantage. We know how to grow, control, and engineer it far beyond jewelry.

**Our ask**

**Today, we're looking for introductions to engineers building hardware that is limited by heat.** 

Specifically:

* AI accelerator packaging teams
* Advanced packaging / OSAT engineers
* Aerospace, space, and defence electronics
* Data-centre infrastructure companies
* High-power RF and GaN teams

Introduce us to the engineer responsible for the hottest, hardest-to-cool hardware, especially where size, weight, or power makes cooling difficult. 

We’ll build them a custom diamond sample to test.

Email us at [founders@karalabs.ai](mailto:founders@karalabs.ai) or book time here: <https://calendly.com/aarin-berkeley/aarin-jhaveri-s-calender>

**Diamond spent centuries as a symbol of “extraordinary”. We are making it something the world can build with.**

launches.title: Zomma: AI operations employees for finance back offices
launches.tagline: Computer-use agents that work cross-border transaction alert investigations end to end: collect evidence, produce an assessment, draft an RFI.
launches.body:
We're building Zomma: AI operations employees for finance back offices, starting with cross-border transaction alert investigations.

**TL;DR:** Zomma agents work directly inside the software your ops team already uses. No APIs, no integrations. For every cross-border alert, the agent gathers the evidence, writes the draft assessment, and drafts the RFI, end-to-end. Running live compliance-ops pilots with a US RIA and a $10B AUM wealth tech. 92% on OSWorld.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDXDKH_tYhg>

## **The problem**

Cross-border payments trip more monitoring rules than anything else in the queue: sanctions name hits on foreign counterparties, high-risk corridors, first-time beneficiaries. Most alerts are false positives (McKinsey: over 90% in transaction monitoring), but every one still needs to be investigated. 20 to 60 minutes per case, across five or six systems, several with no API at all. And the evidence that clears them sits in foreign company registries and local-language adverse media. 

So review capacity scales the only way it can: hiring. When hiring lags volume, alerts pile into backlogs that take months to clear, and backlogs are what regulators fine: $3.8B in AML penalties last year alone.

## **What Zomma does**

Zomma agents work the queue on the same screens your analysts use: case manager, screening tool, admin panel, inbox, web search. Onboarding looks like hiring: an SOP and a login.

On a transaction monitoring alert, the agent

* pulls the KYC profile and payment history
* verifies the invoice and researches the counterparty, including registries you can only search by hand
* writes a case-specific assessment with every claim cited to the source screen
* drafts the RFI when documents are missing

Every step is logged and replayable: timestamped screenshots of every page checked, numbered citations, explicit no-match statements, a screen-by-screen trail an examiner can follow.

## **Why start with cross-border alerts**

If an employee can do it on a screen, Zomma can learn it: the rest of the compliance queue, payment disputes, client onboarding, trade ops. Cross-border alerts come first because they have the exact shape our agents are best at: high-volume, parallelizable work that needs real reasoning but follows a defined workflow to a documented disposition. They're also the hardest cases to automate any other way: the evidence lives in registries and portals that will never have APIs. And agents scale with the queue: a volume spike means provisioning two more that afternoon; a BPO batch takes a month to train.

Computer-use agents only recently got accurate enough to trust with a live queue, which is why we're building this now. Our state-of-the-art computer-use harness with our procedural and workflow memory system scores 92% on OSWorld.

## **Team**

* **Jihyun (CEO):** founding team at a Blackstone-backed hedge fund, scaled Asia's largest wealth tech, Goldman engineer.
* **Cash (CTO):** backend systems behind $20B+ in yearly transactions, trains VLMs for computer use.
* **Varun (CPO):** high-performance infra at Apple, design-verification agents at Bronco AI (YC S23).

Send us \~100 closed cross-border alerts and we'll show you what the agent would have done with them, or book a call: zommalabs.com/call.

launches.title: Rex: Turn enterprise order-to-cash into an autonomous operation
launches.tagline: AI Operations Partner for Enterprise Order to Cash
launches.body:
Rex is an AI service that runs order-to-cash and accounts receivable operations for enterprises. Founders [Merlin Kafka](https://www.linkedin.com/in/merlinkafka/) and [Lewis Blackwood](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisblackwood) spent 4 years at an a16z-backed startup helping finance teams at startups like Cognition, Legora and Bridge automate revenue collection. The problem is 100x bigger in the enterprise, so they built Rex: agents that do the work end-to-end. Live in production with Synthesia.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BKS7qaZS8Is>

**Revenue ≠ cash**

Enterprises invoice customers, then spend months chasing the money through email chains, PDFs and ancient web portals. A $1M invoice sits unpaid because one PO number didn't match.

Multiply that across thousands of customers and you get 100+ person teams, often offshore, doing this by hand: collections, invoice submission, dispute resolution, deduction management, cash application. Order-to-cash is the most outsourced process in finance because the work needs judgment. Reading a customer's email and deciding whether their dispute is valid. Working out which of 14 open invoices a lump-sum payment covers. Knowing that this account always pays late but always pays, and that one needs escalating now.

AR automation software has existed for 20 years and the teams never got smaller, because the tools organise the work while people still do it. Businesses invoice each other tens of trillions of dollars a year; the labour and outsourcing spend on collecting it is over $100B. Until now the only way to scale was headcount or a BPO contract.

**What Rex does**

Rex connects to the ERP (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle), CRM (Salesforce), billing system and shared AR inbox, and learns how the team runs the process today. That knowledge becomes editable agent operating procedures: how to chase a Fortune 500 buyer vs a startup, which deductions get investigated vs written off, when a dispute goes to a human.

Then agents run those procedures across thousands of accounts in parallel:

* Collections and payment follow-ups, including the long tail no team gets to
* Invoice submission and status tracking inside procurement portals (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Tungsten and hundreds of others)
* Dispute and deduction investigation
* Remittance processing and cash application
* Responding to customer finance emails
* Updating ERP, CRM and billing records
* Routing exceptions to the team for approval

Portals deserve a special mention: an increasing share of enterprise invoices must be submitted and tracked inside the buyer's procurement system. It's the work AR teams hate most and the work software vendors ignore. Rex treats it as core.

**Is Rex a managed service or software?**

Enterprises can partner with Rex as a managed service provider or let their team operate Rex. AR software (dunning tools, collections worklists, AR dashboards) organises work for a team to do. Rex agents do the work, and the finance team approves exceptions. With Rex, the team stops drowning in routine chasing and handles the judgment calls. Customers compare Rex to their next AR hire, their offshore team, or their BPO contract.

**Can finance teams trust AI agents with collections?**

Autonomy is earned, not switched on. Each procedure starts supervised: Rex proposes, the team approves. Once a procedure hits its accuracy bar for the account, it graduates and runs autonomously. Safe, high-volume work goes first; judgment-heavy edges stay gated as long as the team wants. Every action is logged with its full reasoning, so finance audits the system instead of babysitting it.

**Traction**

[Rex is live in production with enterprises like Synthesia](https://www.rex.inc/customers/synthesia), running collections, portal submissions, inbox triage and cash application. Cases that used to take weeks of back and forth resolve in minutes.

**Get in touch**

If invoice volume is outgrowing the finance team, or order-to-cash runs on offshore headcount or a BPO contract, get in touch: [rex.inc](http://rex.inc)

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Studio is a simulation lab studying how humans and societies interact with new ideas, and building the first software models that can accurately predict that response. Instead of creating digital twins of survey respondents, Studio builds live market models of interconnected consumer segments from real behavior data. Studio's predictions match live KPI outcomes like revenue and sentiment with over 95% accuracy.

<https://youtu.be/g0M-T2ohtcQ>

## The problem

A huge number of consequential decisions are bets on human behavior.

A company launches a product or changes a price. A brand runs a campaign. A public institution launches a new initiative or communications strategy. In each case, the outcome depends on how a population responds.

Today, teams rely on surveys and historical data to help derisk those bets.

But those tools are inherently outdated and non-comprehensive: they observe people individually and at a point in time.

_Real populations don’t behave that way._

People influence one another. Reactions spread between groups. Adoption compounds or fades. Sentiment changes. A decision that resonates with one audience can change how another audience responds. Those interactions are what ultimately determine outcomes like revenue, conversion, adoption, and sentiment.

Currently, the only real “simulation” is the launch itself.

## What we do

Studio builds live models of a company’s market from real data on how consumers behave. It overlays internal data like sales and campaign performance with external evidence like social conversations and market trends.

Studio uses those signals to construct highly specific audience cohorts and model how their behavior and influence interact over time.

Teams can then:

* **Test-run launches:** see how a new product, price, campaign, message, or initiative will unfold.
* **Forecast outcomes:** revenue, conversion, adoption, sentiment, and other KPIs.
* **Understand why:** know which groups drive the result, by how much, and trace outcomes to exact evidence.
* **Test alternatives:** compare different versions of a decision to find the optimal variation.
* **Improve over time:** compare forecasts with real outcomes and recalibrate the model.

Instead of predicting “How will this person respond to X?”, Studio answers:

“How will a population interact with X, and why?”

Studio has live-tested with large consumer brands like Danone and Mila, and our model’s predictions match real-world KPI outcomes with >95% accuracy.

## Why we built it

We’ve spent years predicting behavior. Nikita built simulation software to understand and predict individual decision-making at MIT, while Cameron built predictive models for financial institutions and in private equity, and agent-based society simulations at UC Berkeley MET.

We met at the same gap: you can simulate how a protein will fold or how a financial system will react to a market shock, but there is no equivalent for simulating how society will interact with a new idea. We’re now creating a studio to design society.

## Where we’re starting

We’re initially working with enterprises making high-stakes audience-facing decisions across product, pricing, innovation, brand, marketing, and communications.

But the underlying problem is much broader.

Any organization trying to create a particular response in a population should be able to test different versions of that decision, understand how reactions might spread, and compare likely outcomes before deploying it.

## Our ask

We’d love to talk to teams making consumer-facing decisions. This could be a new product, pricing plan, campaign, etc.

If you have an upcoming decision you’d like to test before it goes live, we’d love to run it through Studio!

launches.body:
Hey everyone, we're Mathieu, Thomas and Nicolas, two brothers and a best friend building COACH.

**TL;DR:** We're building the best coach for in-person sales ever built: reps record every in-person meeting from our app, and our AI turns it into precise, personalized coaching. And it works so well that 5 months in, thousands of reps already run on COACH, and we're live with the top 5 in-person sales companies in France, lifting conversion rates by 32% on average.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yJB7wC3ddTM>

## The Problem

85% of sales in the world happen face-to-face. And in-person selling is brutally hard: a rep alone in someone's living room, reading signals, handling doubts, feeling the exact moment to push.

The best reps catch what no playbook can teach. That's why 20% of them bring in 80% of the revenue, and nobody knows what they're doing differently. The only way to find out is to physically be there: a ride-along, a full day, 100 km of driving to watch a single meeting. It doesn't scale.

## The Solution

COACH's AI learns how to close customers for your business, and closes the gap at every layer of the sales org:

* **Every rep gets a personal coach:** they record every in-person meeting from our mobile app, in-home, showroom, door-to-door, and walk out of each one with personal, precise feedback and a clear path to the next close. Our AI learns from your top 20% and coaches everyone to perform like them, starting each day with a morning brief on their weakest point. 90% improve on it in their first week.
* **The company gets a sales brain that learns how to close its customers:** every meeting feeds it. Why is one region closing twice as much as another? Which objection is killing deals this month? Leadership just asks, COACH has the answer.

Thousands of reps already run on COACH, live with the top 5 in-person sales companies in France, where we've lifted conversion rates by 32% on average, and dozens of reps 3–4×'d their numbers. We're now growing fast in the USA, where our first customers are switching from virtual ride-along platforms to COACH.

Every rep gets a coach. Your company gets a brain.

## The Team

At 18 and 21, we built Alsace Test: a 44-rep field sales team that did €3.5M in 14 months. Alsace made us fall in love with in-person sales, obsessed, actually.

And one thing was driving us crazy: same product, same material, same training, and one guy closed 4× more than the others. We were driving 2,000 km a week just to watch reps sell.

So we asked them to record themselves. Suddenly, without moving, we were listening to 10 hours of meetings a day. That was COACH before COACH.

In an AI-driven sales world, we're deeply convinced Zoom sales and call centers will soon be replaced by AI agents. Face-to-face selling will be the last human job on Earth. We're betting on it.

## Our Ask

If you run 5+ field sales reps, let's talk, we'll show you how to make them superhuman.

launches.body:
Hey everyone! I'm Nikos, the founder of Glen.

**TL;DR**

Glen is building the organizational learning and context layer for agents.

Every agent session your team runs produces reasoning worth keeping, and nearly all of it is discarded the moment the window closes.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T0CkjYfo3k3FB40_R7UPNfONO-SdgfKB](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T0CkjYfo3k3FB40_R7UPNfONO-SdgfKB/view?usp=sharing)

Glen is the layer that unifies every agent and model your company run. Glen pulls in agent sessions from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, plus Slack messages, GitHub prs, tickets, docs and calls. When a new agent picks up a task, Glen finds relevant prior context and injects it in the agents context window to steer it, producing knowledge work that is significantly higher quality, faster and cheaper than ever before.

And Glen does more. It unifies all of your org's context: query the original agent behind any line of code, search every session your org has ever run, dynamic skill distillation, multiplayer agents, unified transcripts you can hand between Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor mid-task, and a company brain in Slack.\
\
Composio scaled usage from 2 users to org wide. Over a dozen SF startups use Glen. I’m onboarding new teams every week, email me at [nikos@tryglen.com](mailto:nikos@tryglen.com) to get set up with early access.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111187&key=user_uploads/3237090/2d8c514f-6318-491a-937e-87f1d3e32ae6)

**What Glen does practically**

* Relevant context injected on every prompt which steers your model to do knowledge work more efficiently saving your time, money and headaches. These injections can consist or niche knowledge unique to the repo you are working in, high level understanding of relevant sub systems, and previous approaches teammates took to similar problems. Glen surfaces the prior work that matters automatically, so tasks finish faster and cost fewer tokens with no loss in quality, because what lands in the window is the relevant work rather than more of it. You can lazy-prompt instead of retyping the same background every session. So far, internal evals show about a **29% reduction in token spend** and **21% reduction in task completion time**.

  \
  **Also…**
* PR review with the original context. Highlight any code in a diff and ask why it's there. Glen queries the agent session that produced it and answers from the actual trace instead of guessing from the diff.
* Code search across every agent trace. Ask your coding agent anything about the codebase and it searches every session any agent in your org has run, so the answer comes from the work that produced the code.
* A skill library the whole org shares. Glen distills what your team does into skills, publishes them where everyone can use them, and surfaces the right one automatically when someone hits a task it covers.
* Multiplayer agents. You and your designer work the same deck in parallel, you on copy and them on design. Make a design edit and your agent applies the style theirs has learned. When they touch the copy, their agent writes in the voice yours was taught. Neither of you hands anything off.
* No lock-in to a model provider. Transcripts from Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor all land in one place, and you can hand a session from one to another mid-task, with Glen converting the format so the next agent picks up exactly where the last one stopped. Your context, your skills, and your shared artifacts come with you, so moving between providers costs nothing.
* We have a Slackbot company brain too!

**Deployed org-wide at Composio**. Composio was my first design partner. It started with two users, grew to about twenty naturally as I iterated on the product, and is now used across the company. Also in use at over a dozen other companies!

In the last 30 days alone, Glen injected **10s of millions of** characters of organizational context into their agents. These injections steer the models used by these teams, giving them a competative edge that allows them to perform knowledge work better, faster, and cheaper.

**My Ask**

If you are at a startup and are reading this, there's a 80% chance Glen would be a great addition to your productivity stack. Most teams run agents heavily, and if yours is tired of re-explaining meetings, Slack, tickets, conventions, and what past sessions already worked out, that's exactly what Glen removes. \
\
I'd love to chat, and I'll come to your office, or wherever you are, and set you up for a with a early access workspace before public availability. Just shoot me an email at [nikos@tryglen.com](mailto:nikos@tryglen.com)!

launches.tagline: Replacing the fragmented hotel tech stack with one system that can understand and run hotel operations.
launches.body:
Hi everyone, we're Axel, Oscar, Jon, and Douglas, founders of Zaplar.

**TL;DR:** Zaplar is an agentic hotel OS that replaces the fragmented hotel tech stack (PMS, booking engine, channel manager, POS, revenue management, housekeeping, and more) with one system built from the ground up for AI. We're eight people with backgrounds in hotel operations, engineering, AI research, and cybersecurity.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/c7720ef9-5a08-43eb-9631-4fefb2d239b6)

**Ask:** Intros to hotel owners and operators who are unhappy with their PMS, and to executives and C-suite at hotel groups planning their next core system replacement. Details at the bottom. Reach us at [founders@zaplar.com](mailto:founders@zaplar.com).

[Launch Video!](https://youtu.be/bpfJATRnYQM)

## The problem

Incumbents are bolting AI onto systems built for a different era. They provide a layer of AI to the end user, but the automations beneath it stay constrained. Their claim to use AI is correct. They just can't reason across the operation or automate work end to end.

No existing PMS or bolt-on solution gives hotels the architecture AI actually requires. And even if one did, a PMS alone still wouldn't automate hotel operations. It's one of as many as 15 systems a hotel runs, each built on a different architecture, each focused on one part of the operation, none able to act beyond its own boundaries.

AI can't run a hotel if it can't understand the hotel.

To unlock the full potential of AI, a hotel has to run on a single system with a unified architecture: one that lets AI reason across the entire property, free of the boundaries integrations create and the context each one isolates behind them. Incumbents can't build this without replacing the foundation their business depends on, and they won't.

We arrived at this the slow way. Douglas's family has spent their careers running hotels, and we first built Zaplar to solve event bookings for them. In demo after demo, hotels were already evaluating another PMS, including ones that had just switched. Even leading vendors did not make a product hotels wanted to use.

## The solution

Zaplar was built on this thesis from the start: the first truly AI-native operating system for hotels. It’s the path of most resistance, but the only way to do it right.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/5a0f8f2c-bcb0-4ebc-a3e1-e2c30c80baec)

Zaplar spatially maps out the entire property and its resources so that AI agents can reason across the hotel and understand how everything connects. On top of this architecture sit a PMS, POS, channel manager, booking engine, guest portal, housekeeping system, and more, with no boundaries between them. The result is an autonomous system that works in the background and completes work on its own. The system surfaces suggestions for staff to review, edit, and approve.

Our goal is to be vertically integrated. Beyond deeper automation and richer context, the greatest benefit is that we can put all our effort into staying at the forefront, because we're not constrained by what anyone else is doing. Major hotel groups are starting to replace their aging systems, and we intend to be the only option on the table designed for what comes after.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107463&key=user_uploads/3037509/ad3b8b01-9f05-41f1-877e-952a35dc8e8a)

## Our ask

**Hotel owners and operators.** If you own or operate a hotel that is unhappy with its PMS, we would love to talk directly.

**Executives and C-suite at hotel groups.** This is the intro we want most. Anyone at the VP level or above at a group, especially COOs, CIOs, CTOs, and heads of operations or commercial, and above all anyone whose group is planning a core system replacement in the next 18 months.

**Everyone else.** You do not need to know their software situation to make the intro useful. We are focused on independents, small and mid-size groups, and boutique and luxury properties. If you have stayed somewhere you loved, send us the name and we will take it from there.

Reach us at [founders@zaplar.com](mailto:founders@zaplar.com) or learn more at [zaplar.com](http://zaplar.com).

launches.body:
screenpipe records what you do, see and hear on your computer, makes it searchable, and gives agents the context to understand how you actually work. The project has 20K+ GitHub stars.

<https://youtu.be/c1jV6E9pyug>

Most AI agents start every task with partial context.

They can read the prompt and apps you connect. They do not remember the meeting where a decision was made, the tab you opened last Tuesday, the exact steps you took to fix a problem, or the edge case you discovered while doing the work.

screenpipe runs quietly in the background and captures screen and audio context on your machine. Then you can ask:

* maintain a second brain for every person, projects, tasks, meetings


* turn the workday into a daily recap and time breakdown for standups or client billing
* maintain a personal CRM from the people, conversations, and follow-ups seen during the day
* find commitments mentioned in meetings or messages that never made it into a task list
* analyze repeated work and produce a list of workflows worth automating
* save prompts and context from Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT into a searchable journal

Agents can use screenpipe as long-term memory, so they work from what actually happened instead of only what you remembered to paste into a prompt.

The same foundation also works across team machines. Teams can map repeated workflows, generate SOPs, find bottlenecks, and identify automation opportunities across the tools where work actually happens.

screenpipe is open source and local-first. You control what gets recorded, can exclude apps, windows, and URLs, and choose where your data lives.

I’ve been building my own AI second brain since 2020, but it could only remember what I explicitly saved. I built screenpipe so my AI could understand what I was actually doing across my screen and conversations. Other people began using it for the same reason. Today, we’re turning that foundation into context for personal and team agents.

**Our ask**

Try screenpipe and comment with the agent you would build if it could remember everything you’ve worked on.

Try screenpipe: <https://screenpipe.com>
