name: Aerogen Systems
long_description:
We are building the future of chip manufacturing.

Chips are more advanced than ever, and the features inside them keep getting smaller. But the cleanroom infrastructure supporting their manufacture has not scaled at the same pace. Intel, TSMC, Samsung, and others spend billions building and operating massive cleanrooms, only to isolate their most advanced wafers from the surrounding facility as much as possible.

We think that architecture is backwards. Instead of making the entire building cleaner, why not make the machinery itself as clean as possible?

Talos is our proprietary tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor equipment and continuously destroys airborne molecular contaminants before they reach the wafer. Instead of fighting contamination by constantly flooding tools with ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos keeps the environment inside the machine 10–100x cleaner, without the massive purge-gas bill.

Talos is powerful on its own, but it is also the foundation for a much bigger vision: the Cleanpipe.

The Aerogen Systems Cleanpipe is an ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Rather than relying on a billion-dollar cleanroom to protect every cubic foot of factory space, Cleanpipe creates a controlled environment only where cleanliness actually matters: around the wafer.

Talos cleans the tools. Cleanpipe connects them. Eventually, we delete the cleanroom and build more advanced chips, at greater scale, with radically less infrastructure. With cleanpipes connecting tools, chip fabs can exist anywhere.
one_liner: Modernizing Chip Manufacturing Infrastructure

launches.title: Aerogen Systems: Building Chip Fabs Without Cleanrooms
launches.tagline: Redefining the architecture behind chip manufacturing
launches.body:
Hi YC!

We’re [Noah](https://www.linkedin.com/in/noahvogel/) and [Colin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/colin-lavery-67b7512a3/), the founders of [Aerogen Systems](https://www.aerogensystems.com/). We’re building the next generation of clean infrastructure for chip manufacturing.

**TL;DR:** Aerogen Systems makes semiconductor tools clean themselves. Talos, our tool-integrated purification system, continuously destroys airborne contaminants around the wafer, creating 10–100x cleaner tool environments while reducing dependence on ultra-high-purity nitrogen. Over time, Talos becomes the foundation for the Cleanpipe, an ultra-clean interconnect network that lets wafers move between tools without depending on the surrounding cleanroom.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5yBzBCzwFV8>

# **The Problem**

**Chip features keep getting smaller, but cleanrooms do not scale with them.**

Semiconductor manufacturers spend billions building enormous cleanroom facilities, then spend even more trying to isolate their most advanced wafers from the environment they just built.

As features approach the atomic scale, trace airborne contaminants that were once tolerable can create defects, reduce yield, and disrupt some of the most sensitive manufacturing processes on Earth. Yet the industry's answer has largely been more of the same: cleaner facilities, more filtration, and more ultra-high-purity nitrogen flooding sensitive equipment.

**The proof is in the yield numbers.** 2026 reporting puts Intel’s 18A program between roughly 50% and 65% yield as it pushed the node toward high-volume production. With global semiconductor sales projected to reach **$1.5 trillion** in 2026, every percentage point matters. Improvements in yield and manufacturing efficiency can represent tens of billions of dollars in value.

# **The Solution**

At Aerogen Systems, we think the industry is approaching this problem backwards.

**The whole factory does not need to be a massive cleanroom.** Only the environment immediately surrounding the wafer does.

Talos is our proprietary, tool-integrated purification system. It sits directly inside semiconductor manufacturing equipment and continuously recirculates and purifies the environment around the wafer. Instead of constantly replacing contaminated gas with more ultra-high-purity nitrogen, Talos destroys contaminants at the point of use, offering 10–100x cleaner tool environments while dramatically reducing dependence on purge gas and consumable filtration.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a095a4e2-31a2-4307-b8f1-bca417cb27d7)

_1. Rendering of standalone Talos unit._

But Talos is only part of the vision.

With tool-integrated purification units as a foundation, we build **the Cleanpipe: ultra-clean interconnect infrastructure** that protects wafers as they move from machine to machine across the fab. Talos cleans the tools. The Cleanpipe connects tools to each other. Together, they delete the cleanroom and all the expenses that come with it.

# **What We’ve Built**

Talos has progressed through multiple generations of hardware development and is protected by patent-pending IP. We’ve validated the core purification architecture and are now working toward tool integrations, pilots, and commercial deployments with semiconductor manufacturers and equipment companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/a8596c2c-c29b-4271-8d92-85672dce0dc1)

_2. Test results showing Talos bringing industry-standard 6N purification levels down to 8N — a 100x improvement in cleanliness._

The next step is connecting these purified environments together through the Cleanpipe, creating an ultra-clean path around the wafer from tool to tool and ultimately removing the need to maintain the entire fab as one enormous cleanroom.

# **The Team**

Aerogen Systems started as a NASA-backed research group at the University of Michigan, where our team developed the underlying purification technology. 

We have spent the last several years designing, testing, patenting, and rebuilding this technology for extreme manufacturing environments.

* Noah, CEO, worked in manufacturing engineering at SpaceX, where he focused on production rate and yield improvement for the Starship program.


* Colin, CTO, previously built advanced particle detectors at H3D and led the team through the earliest design cycles of Talos.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111026&key=user_uploads/3388722/4db2a255-30a8-44ee-928b-b07425918094)

# **Our Ask**

We want to meet semiconductor fabs, equipment OEMs, and manufacturing teams interested in pilots, tool integrations, and commercial deployments. If this sounds like you, please reach out to [hi@aerogensystems.com](mailto:hi@aerogensystems.com)!

We are building toward a world where fabs no longer need billion-dollar cleanrooms to manufacture the world’s most advanced chips.

\
Whitespace is the AI operating system for wholesale distributors. It connects to their systems to build a living model of their business, then deploys self-improving AI agents to do work like inventory planning, customer service, and order processing.

**Problem**

Wholesale distribution is a $60 trillion global industry that touches one in every five dollars of global output. Yet it still runs largely manually. At a typical wholesale distributor, 30-50% of staff are dedicated to back-office tasks.

They spend their days on email, spreadsheets, and legacy systems, relying on tribal knowledge in their heads. Businesses cannot scale without hiring, and training a new hire takes >6 months.

A quote from one of our customers really brings this to life: “I have 6 reps typing 600 lines of orders from email into the ERP every day. Everyone is inside our ERP and spreadsheets, copying data from one place to another.”

**Solution**

Whitespace is the AI operating system for wholesale distributors. It connects to their systems to build a living model of their business, then deploys self-improving AI agents. 

We’re already working with wholesale distributors in sectors including industrial supplies and building materials to set up agents for processes like:

* **Inventory Planning.** Forecasts product demand, recommends reorder quantities against stock levels, and learns over time from actual demand.
* **Customer Service.** Monitors inboxes for support queries, digs through systems to find answers, and responds with human oversight.
* **Order Processing.** Monitors inboxes, enters orders into the ERP, flags exceptions to humans, and learns from their corrections.

<https://youtu.be/4UxlKKXrgfI?si=EwGhX1LCTGyauuw6>

**Team**

Both our families ran wholesale distribution businesses, so we grew up seeing the inefficiencies and the opportunities firsthand.

launches.tagline: GitNexus gives coding agents a map of your codebase, so they stop burning tokens looking for it.
launches.body:
##### We're building the most token-efficient coding agent in the world. The reason it works is GitNexus, our open-source knowledge graph for your codebase.

<https://youtu.be/-ErU4cCRSlQ>

##### The problem

Coding agents don't understand your repo. They grep, they guess, they re-read the same files, and they stuff half your codebase into a context window hoping the answer is in there somewhere. You pay for every one of those tokens, and the agent still misses the cross-file relationship that mattered.

The bottleneck isn't the model. It's context.

##### What we built:

GitNexus indexes your repository into a knowledge graph (symbols, call paths, imports, ownership, history) and serves the agent exactly the context a task needs, instead of everything it might need.

It's one connected stack:

* The knowledge graph. Run npx gitnexus analyze and you have it
* A coding agent that runs on top of it
* Automated PR review grounded in the same graph

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110659&key=user_uploads/1607382/1d3e51af-d3b5-4ee6-b0c3-b80bc4337c3e)

##### The proof:

On the DeepSWE benchmark, we ran the same agent with our graph and without it:

* 37% to 68.4% pass rate. Nearly twice the bugs solved
* Half the cost per fix, with fewer tokens
* On the hardest tasks, the gap more than triples

Full methodology and results: <https://www.akonlabs.com/benchmarks>

##### Where we are:

* 45,000+ GitHub stars
* 65,000 weekly npm downloads
* 10+ enterprises onboarded

##### About the team:

Subham Kundu and Abhigyan Patwari have spent nearly half a decade working on knowledge graphs. Between them, they've been founding engineers, CTOs, and principal AI engineers, taking products from 0 to 100 at multiple startups. Subham is a seasoned engineer who has scaled products to millions of users, won multiple hackathons, and doing a PhD in reinforcement learning. Abhigyan is a seasoned technologist and serial open source contributor, with involvement across multiple open source projects.

##### Run it in your way:

Managed, or fully sovereign. Self-hosted, air-gapped, nothing leaves your network.

##### Looking to cut your coding agent bill?

If you want to lower your coding agent spend without giving up frontier performance, sign up at <https://www.akonlabs.com>. We'll get you set up on your own repo and show you the before-and-after on your actual token costs.

##### Our other asks

* Try the open-source version. Run npx gitnexus analyze. Takes a minute
* Intros. Engineering leaders where agent cost or code-context quality is a real line item, especially in regulated or air-gapped environments
* Tell us where it breaks. Weird monorepos and polyglot repos are the most useful feedback we get

launches.title: Vendo: Let Your Users Build Their Own Features on Top of Your Product

launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋 We're Nour and Yousef, co-founders of Vendo.

**TL;DR:** Vendo is the customization layer that lets your users build their own features and micro-apps right inside your product, on your existing API and within your brand and guardrails.. Plug it into the agent you already have, or drop in a production-ready one, with a single command. It's open source.

**Try it now:** [vendo.run](http://vendo.run) \
**Star us on Github**: <https://github.com/runvendo/vendo>

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JjtDhA7DZw8>

## **The Problem**

Every product team is drowning in the same thing: a feature backlog that never ends. Different customers want different things, and you can't build a thousand versions of your product. So most requests sit in a board for months, and the customer who asked churns quietly because your product doesn't do the one thing they needed.

The AI wave made this worse, not better. Everyone knows their product should be agent-native, but building a real agent (one that can take actions, generate UI, remember context, and stay inside your security guardrails) takes serious engineering hours and ongoing maintenance. So most teams ship a chatbot bolted to the corner of the screen and call it AI. Users don't want another chatbot. They want your product to do the exact thing they need.

## **How Vendo Works**

Vendo installs into your product with one command. It reads your theme, your components, and your API surface. From then on, your users can describe what they want in plain English and Vendo builds it for them, live, inside your app:

* **Personalize the product** to exactly how each user works, in your own design system.
* **Build automations** that run on a schedule and take real actions in your product.
* **Pull in hundreds of external tools**, so the workflow doesn't stop at your app's edge.

Everything runs in secure sandboxes and inside your existing security guardrails. The agent only ever has the same access the user has, so it can't do anything they couldn't already do themselves, and your source code never gets touched.

You can plug Vendo into the agent you already have, or get a production-ready one out of the box with actions, UI generation, and a knowledge base included. It's completely open source, and it takes one command to install and push live to your users.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106667&key=user_uploads/2705364/5b5c05c6-3415-4d23-bf67-a779d56456c7)

## **Who We Are**

We're a Stanford and Berkeley team who’ve known each other since kindergarten and previously built in-store AI shopping assistants for retailers.

* **Nour (CEO)** studied Mechanical Engineering at Berkeley and interned as a mechanical design engineer. Before startups, he played professional academy soccer for the San Jose Earthquakes for 7 years.
* **Yousef (CTO)** graduated high school at 15 and completed a Bachelor’s in EECS from Berkeley and a Master’s from Stanford. He previously built FPGA infrastructure at Apple and worked on chip design at AMD.

### **Our Ask**

* **If you run a product team** and your backlog is full of "can it also do X" requests, we want to talk. We'll integrate Vendo for you.
* **If you're a developer** who wants the best open-source way to put a real agent into your product, come try it and tell us what breaks.
* **Intros welcome** to any company feeling the request pain who wants an agentic interface on top of their product.

Reach us at [vendo.run](http://vendo.run) or [nour@vendo.run](mailto:nour@vendo.run)

launches.tagline: Deploy AI that owns complete jobs and are measured against predefined outcomes and KPIs. Tenor's AI operates across your tools and improves its decisions with every outcome to drive better results.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:**

The defining resource of the internet was page views. The defining resource of AI is tokens. But while companies can measure exactly what their tokens cost, they still can’t easily tell what those tokens produced. \
Tenor connects the two. Every piece of AI work starts with an outcome and a budget. Tenor tracks the resources spent against the result produced, learns from that result, and helps determine where the next tokens should go.\
That’s the bigger opportunity: not just attributing AI spend, but allocating machine intelligence toward what creates value. Once a company knows where its tokens make money, it can do more of what works, less of what doesn’t, and continuously reshape itself around where AI creates value.

## 🤯 The Problem

While companies have become good at measuring AI consumption, they still can’t tell what that intelligence produced in business value.\
\
The internet went through a similar transition.

Its defining resource was page views. Early on, advertisers could buy impressions and measure exposure. Search advertising changed the model by connecting spend to intent and outcomes. Google then turned that into an engine for allocating dollars toward what performed.

AI is still early in that transition. Companies deploy copilots, agents, and automations across the organization. Each produces activity and consumes tokens. But the economic context usually lives somewhere else.

What was this intelligence supposed to accomplish? What changed because it ran? Was the outcome worth what it cost? Should the next token go here or somewhere else?

Without those answers, AI remains largely a software expense: something companies buy and monitor rather than a resource they can economically allocate.

And the bigger loss isn’t wasted tokens. It’s lost learning.

Millions of pieces of work happen, outcomes disappear into different systems, and very little of that experience determines how the next unit of intelligence gets deployed.

### ⚙️ The Solution

Tenor starts with the outcome.

Before intelligence is deployed, the work gets an economic identity: what it owns, what success means, what it can spend, which systems it can act on, and when humans need to intervene.

Now every token is spent in service of something measurable.

So instead of: This agent consumed X.

You can ask: What did X produce?

That closes the loop: allocate → work → outcome → attribute → learn → reallocate

Attribution tells you what worked. Allocation is what makes that knowledge valuable.

Work that produces value can receive more intelligence. Work that doesn’t can be changed, rebuilt, or stopped. Every outcome improves the next allocation decision.

Over time, that feedback loop reaches beyond individual workflows.

Responsibilities move. Processes disappear. New ones emerge. Software changes around the work. The organization gradually restructures itself around where machine intelligence produces the greatest value.

That’s what we’re building Tenor for: not just to measure the token economy, but to give companies the machinery to operate inside it.

## 👋 Team

Muhtasham Oblokulov — AI researcher, 3,000+ citations, ICML-published. Former Senior ML Engineer at Munich Re, where his models drove $1B in revenue.

Hamze Al-Zamkan — President of [TUM.ai](http://TUM.ai), which he grew into Europe's largest student-led AI organization and a talent pipeline for Munich's AI ecosystem. Deployed AI systems at appliedAI, and worked on growth at Voggt and Terra. Studied CS at TUM and CDTM.

Amgad Al-Zamkan — Studied CS at TUM and UC Berkeley. Researched adaptive decision systems. Automated judgment-heavy work at Amazon.

launches.body:
**TLDR:** Risklytics is a commercial insurance brokerage for companies building with AI in the physical space, from robot fleets on customer sites to agents running in production. This year many insurance companies stopped covering risks that involve AI. We find the insurers that will still cover it, translate what you're building into terms they can price, and read every clause before anything is signed.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jHTzpKbmZa4>

**The problem**

Starting this year, many insurance companies began excluding coverage for injury and property damage arising out of AI.

For a hardtech company that language reaches everything you do. If AI touched the work anywhere, including the tools your engineers designed it with or the product itself, the insurer can deny the claim.

The problem with these exclusions is that they get added account by account, so the same hardware can be covered at one insurer and excluded at the next, and nothing in the process makes that obvious. It shows up as a form number on the endorsement list attached to your renewal, which is why most founders don't learn they have one until they file a claim.

**Why now**

Physical AI is scaling faster than the insurance market underneath it. Insurance moves slower, and its first instinct with an unfamiliar risk is to exclude it and wait for loss data. Cyber went the same way: exclusions first, then specialists who understood it, then a real market. AI is at the exclusion stage now, and these companies pushing the frontier can't wait for the cycle to finish on its own. 

**What we do**

We handle the whole coverage process end to end.

You send us an application. We take what you're building and put it in terms an insurance company can understand and price.

Then we go to market. We have access to hundreds of insurance companies, the ones that actually write this kind of risk, and we take your file to them. Most will pass. The few that want it compete on price and terms, and we keep shopping until every requirement you have is met, including the limits your customer contracts demand.

When offers come back we read the policies line by line. If an AI exclusion is attached, we push to get it removed, or we find a company that writes the AI coverage in on purpose. Then we tell you in plain terms what you've got.

We cover the lines your company actually needs: general liability, umbrella, property, equipment in transit and on customer sites, workers' comp, professional liability, management liability, and cyber.

You never pay us. The insurance company pays us a commission out of the premium when a policy is placed, so applying costs you nothing and there's no additional fee from us at any point.

**Where this goes**

Physical AI is expanding faster than any industry, and every company in it buys insurance every year for as long as it exists. The programs grow as the fleets grow.

We want to be the brokerage that grows with them: the people who know this risk best, hold the relationships with the markets that write it, and build the loss data of the future.

**Why us**

We're Sam and Alex, on leave from Harvard. We were already in insurance building models when we noticed that batch mates building some of the most innovative technology in the world couldn't get covered at all. Since then we’ve landed partnerships to offer these frontier companies easier access to better policies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=110197&key=user_uploads/2666435/74c5c462-a2ff-44b8-ac6c-f8ebc7807dbd)


**The ask**

If you're building anything on the frontier, apply at[ risklytics.ai](http://risklytics.ai). It takes a few minutes, it costs nothing, and we'll come back with what the market says.

It doesn't matter what you have in place today. If you're building, we want to get you covered.

And if you're an insurer, MGA or wholesaler with appetite here, we want to talk:[ risklytics.ai/markets](https://www.risklytics.ai/markets/)

launches.title: Neuromorphic - Building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy
launches.tagline: We make robots smarter, and faster to deploy. Starting with wet labs!
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We’re Cem, Ege, and Vatan, the founders of Neuromorphic 👋\
\
**TL;DR** Neuromorphic is building an embodiment-agnostic “brain” that makes robots fast to deploy, and easy to manage through natural interfaces like Slack, email, and phone. Our goal is to make deploying robots in wet labs and other physical industries as easy as onboarding a new employee.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6T0BDyjakmo>\
\
**The Problem**\
To make robotics mainstream, we believe two problems have to be resolved:\
1\. Deployment: Robots are still too slow, expensive, and engineering-intensive to deploy and adapt to new tasks and environments.\
2\. Interaction: Managing and controlling robots remains too technical.\
\
**What We’ve Built**\
Neuromorphic packages sensors, compute, and software into a “brain” that can be attached to any robot body. An onboard LLM orchestrator turns natural-language instructions into workflows made up of reusable robotic skills, such as navigating, picking up an object, opening a refrigerator, or inspecting an area. Individual skills can be of various types; they could be AI models we develop, like Vision-Language Models and Video Action Models, or just plain code. Sensor-based safety loops monitor every action to ensure reliable execution.

We are also giving robots emails, phone numbers, and Slack access to make human-robot interaction more intuitive than using dashboards. The robots then respond to queries and take actions using the onboard LLM.\
\
**Traction**\
Within a week of our first conversation with a leading biotechnology company, we deployed our robot in their wet lab, which is capable of operating autonomously 24/7, and already completed over 1500 tasks.\
\
**The Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109550&key=user_uploads/3607343/b28b023b-f328-4c5d-9181-720e96e5b1a3)

\
Cem: Second-time founder and did robotics research at Cambridge University. Previously built LLM routing and training acceleration, and did precision robotics.\
\
Vatan: Maintained multiple open-source robotics libraries, most notably MoveIt, one of the most popular motion-planning frameworks for robotics. Led various teams in robotics startups from Series A to Series C in Japan and Singapore. Deployed over a thousand robots.\
\
Ege: Did Robotics and AI research at Bilkent University. Research fellow at Nanyang Technological University. Published research in top AI and robotics conferences. Won HackMIT in 2024.\
\
Cem and Ege first met as teammates in the FIRST Robotics Competition. They reached out to Vatan for mentorship and robotics advice. We spent the next three years building robots and winning competitions together. We remained close and eventually reunited to start Neuromorphic!\
\
**Ask**\
We're looking for warm intros to wet lab, biotech, and physical-industry operators. If you have a repetitive physical process and have wondered whether a robot could do it, email us at [founders@neuromorphic.vision](mailto:founders@neuromorphic.vision) or [book a call here](https://cal.com/team/neuromorphic/meet-the-founders-of-neuromorphic).

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: We're building a modern tax engine for accountants and fintechs building on tax: a deterministic tax calculation and e-filing core behind a single API, built on the IRS's official e-file infrastructure (MeF).**

## A tax return is math. It should be a function call.

We're Angelo and Akash, and we built Luca IQ, a new tax engine for accounting firms. One set of inputs in, a completed, filed return out in minutes. Not bolted onto decades out desktop software.

For CPA firms, that means more returns per preparer, less spend on labor, and a clean path off 30-year-old desktop software. For the PE groups acquiring and scaling firms, it means real operating leverage on the single most labor-intensive part of the business.

<https://youtu.be/IV5nl7grMxI>

**The problem.** \~95% of US firms file their returns through just four companies, and all of them were built decades ago, for the desktop, and are closed. Firms are stuck running tax season on software that can't scale with them. Every modern AI tax tool just pushes data into that same closed software it can't control. Everyone rebuilt the interface.

**What we built.** A new one, and we're opening it. A key principle: AI never does the tax math. AI and human judgment set the inputs, and a deterministic engine computes the return, with a full audit trail on every number. It's either 100% correct or it's wrong, and only a deterministic engine can promise the former. For firms, that means throughput without giving up accuracy or defensibility.

Our core leverage: we're an **IRS-authorized e-file provider as a Software Developer, Transmitter, and Intermediate Service Provider**, so Luca IQ doesn't just compute the return, it e-files straight to the IRS. That full path, calculation through filing, is what firms can't get from a closed engine today.

**Why now.** The profession is running out of people. 300,000+ accountants have left since 2019, and \~70% of CPAs are near retirement. At the same time, private equity is rolling up firms and pushing hard on margin. The work isn't going away. The people are, and the pressure to do more with fewer preparers has never been higher.

**Who we are.** Angelo (CEO) is a CPA who worked in forensic accounting with the FBI, Wall Street, EY and spent years working at tax firms using the legacy softwares we are now replacing. Akash (CTO) was employee #1 at a fintech data-infrastructure startup and leads engineering.

**What we need:**

* **CPA firms who dread tax season**, We'd love 20 minutes to show you what Luca IQ does for throughput and margin. This is who we build for.
* **PE firms rolling up accounting practices.** If tax prep labor is your biggest cost line, let's talk.
* **Developers and fintechs** who need 1040 calculations or e-filing. The engine is one API call, and you can build on it early.

Reach us at [founders@lucaiq.com](mailto:founders@lucaiq.com).

---

**TLDR:** Levocred AI (YC S26) is an AI-native platform for credit funds, fintechs and banks to automate workflows like back-office tasks, portfolio monitoring, compliance and underwriting. Live across multiple credit teams, running \~$1Bn in receivables through the platform.

\*\*Video:\*\*\
<https://youtu.be/OU_G096YPzo>

The winning teams will scale with token consumption, not headcount. Try it today: <https://www.levocred.ai/trynow>

**The problem**

Credit teams run on data scattered across 5-6 tools (CRM, LMS, data rooms, servicer reports) and endless spreadsheets. So highly-paid analysts become data janitors, copy-pasting between systems and rebuilding the same models — instead of the real job: underwriting and managing risk.

It's the same story across all of an analyst’s workflows (like new deals, monitoring, reporting, workouts). One example: to borrow against a credit facility (it’s like a credit card for fintechs with a limit typically in the $100Ms ), a team produces and verifies compliance certificates by hand. That's hours of Excel every time, so they draw less often than they should, leaving millions on the table.

**What is Levocred?**

Levocred is an AI employee for your credit team. It plugs into your loan tapes, credit agreements, servicer reports, and bank feeds, learns how you work, and runs the workflows your analysts do by hand today.

* Analyzes new deals and drafts the investment memos
* Monitors the portfolio, marks valuations, and answers questions in Slack ("what's our exposure to X?")
* Produces and checks compliance certificates, and handles covenant and LP reporting

Why it works when nothing else has:

* **It's AI-native, not a rules engine.** Older tools only work if you hand-code every rule, so they break on messy, real-world data. Levocred's agents read your actual documents and tapes and reason across them. We already run consumer, fintech, litigation finance, and MCA through the same engine.
* **You stay in control** with full auditability and no waiting on a vendor's engineers
* **It compounds.** Every document you load makes it smarter about your book. That data moat is yours. It’s why usage only grows.

The result: a draw that took a day of Excel takes minutes, monitoring runs continuously instead of monthly, and your team spends its time on judgment, not grunt work.

launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋 - we're Aman and Sarthak, founders of Decawork.\
\
**TL;DR:** AI agents shouldn’t have permanent access to company systems. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into fixed rules or manually approve every step. Decawork trains small, company-specific AI models that approve every agent action in real time, based on company policies and interests, the agent’s task, and its past actions. Access is granted for the task at hand and revoked when it’s done.\
\
Launch video: [Watch it here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SanpHIyFcV4)\
\
🚧 **The Problem & Why now?**\
Companies are putting long-running, more autonomous agents to work on broader tasks and goals. These agents need access to critical company systems, but their actions can be unpredictable and may not serve the company’s interests.

OpenAI’s agents have already hacked Hugging Face during testing with reduced safeguards. Replit’s agent deleted data from a live application’s database.

An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Permanent access lets an agent keep using permissions even when they are no longer appropriate for its task.

As agents take on more work independently, access decisions need to happen in real time. But companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rule or have people manually approve every step.\
\
✅ **How we solve this?**\
Decawork gives AI agents access for the task at hand and revokes it when the task is done.

* Connect your agents. Route API requests and MCP tool calls through Decawork to see activity and manage access in one place.
* Set company policies. Write policies in plain English, specify when human approval is required, and connect your existing identity and IT service management systems.
* Deploy a company-specific policy model. We deploy small models that approve actions in real time using your company’s policies and priorities, task context, and past actions. Your agents do the work. Decawork evaluates each proposed action and enforces the access decision before it runs.

🚀 **Team**\
Sarthak built AI systems at NVIDIA that were deployed at OpenAI and Meta, and worked on enterprise AI agents at Ema.

Aman built the AI compliance platform at Barclays used by internal teams globally, then led product at a consumer AI startup serving 100K+ monthly users, hand-wiring credentials for the agents he shipped.

Every one of those deployments came down to the same questions: what can it access, who approved it, and what did it do? We kept solving agent access by hand - so we quit to build the system we wished we’d had.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109883&key=user_uploads/1632535/0ef2784e-ab45-422f-91b9-960473f11dd5)

🙏 **Our Ask**

* If you’re on an IT team or know someone who’s worried about AI agents accessing or misusing company systems, talk to us: <https://decawork.ai/cal> or [founders@decawork.ai](mailto:founders@decawork.ai)

launches.title: Lamb Labs: Custom Chips for AI Inference
launches.tagline: Co-designed models and silicon: we hardcode the model architecture into chips targeting 20,000+ tokens per second and 63x higher intelligence per watt.
launches.body:
**Hi Everyone!** 

**We’re Niki and Thomas - cofounders of Lamb Labs.**  

**TL;DR: We build custom AI inference chips that run inference at 20,000+ tok/s and 63x higher intelligence per watt than a traditional GPU. Fully local and private by construction, no subscriptions, no API costs.** 

**Our mission: the world’s fastest LLM at the lowest power.** 

<https://youtu.be/MhhY1Dy9ltE?feature=shared>

**Our hot take: AI models are finally getting good enough to hardcode them directly into silicon.** Once you stop treating the chip as a general-purpose GPU and burn a specific model into hardware, inference gets radically faster and cheaper per watt. Most of the industry is still building flexible, general chips. We think that flexibility is exactly what's wasting your energy. So we’re on a mission to reduce the energy footprint of AI. 

**The Problem**

AI is taking power on two fronts: concentrating control of data and intelligence, and consuming ever more electricity to grow. That future scares us, so we're building against it.

Here's the technical root of the waste: **GPUs burn most of their energy during inference moving data, not computing.** LLM/VLM inference is memory-bound, fetching a weight from memory costs \~100–1000x the energy of the arithmetic you do with it. So you underutilize the GPU you paid for: some GPUs only hit 20–40% compute utilization during LLM inference while the rest idles waiting on memory.

Cloud hosting adds its own tax: expensive per-token bills, latency you can't control, network dependencies, and your data leaving your control.

**Our Solution**

We build the model and the chip together. 

The Hardware Layer

* **Custom architecture, RL-tuned.** We built an RL environment that co-designs the chip architecture for a given model, optimizing directly for speed and energy per token.
* **Aggressive quantization.** Removes complex math, which shrinks the size and cost of the chip.
* **Weights on-chip.** The model weights live where the compute is overcoming the memory-bandwidth bottleneck

 

Because everything is hardcoded, it's fully local and secure by construction. No connectivity dependency, nothing leaves the device.

The Software Layer 

Designing the chip led us to solving a fundamental flaw in LLMs so we are now open-sourcing a new model next week, converted from another open source model, to run 2x faster on any hardware. Come back next week for part 2 of our launch to find out more….

**Our Ask**

If you answer "yes" to any of these, we'd love your help:

* **Are you paying for inference in watts, not just dollars?** Neocloud or private DC operators who are power- or hardware-cost-bound rather than demand-bound, talk to us.
* **Do you need inference where the cloud isn't an option?** Private AI deployments, regulated, air-gapped, sovereign, or bandwidth-starved deployments.
* **Do you want to deploy the fastest AI models in your stack?** High frequency trading, agentic workflows 
* **Are you stuck on a thermal or battery budget?** Robotics, wearables, consumer AI hardware where a Jetson-class part is over-provisioned and runs too hot.
* **Can you introduce us to anyone above?** Warm intros are the single most useful thing.

Contact us at [contact@lamb-labs.com](mailto:contact@lamb-labs.com)

launches.tagline: AI that finds and fixes OS-level vulnerabilities across device fleets
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** For companies running large fleets of OS-level endpoints (running GPU clusters, having a network of cloud devices, or deploying on-device), Palisade detects and fixes operating-system vulnerabilities (privilege escalation, remote code execution, memory corruption) that are extremely hard to detect and mitigate without applying AI to kernel-level data (syscalls, eBPF traces, process/memory events, network packets). A fix that used to take weeks to roll out, Palisade now applies in minutes across every endpoint.

Hey YC! I'm Prince, an ML researcher and engineer who dropped out from Caltech at 18 to build Palisade.

**What’s the problem:** Modern attacks increasingly target the operating system, but most security products only observe the network, cloud, or application layers. That leaves OS vulnerabilities among the hardest problems to detect and the slowest to remediate across a fleet.

**Why I’m building this:** Since I was 16, I have done plenty of professional red-team and blue-team security work. One pattern kept showing up: OS-level vulnerabilities were consistently the hardest to handle. Detection required low-level visibility, and even after identifying a vulnerability, rolling out a mitigation across hundreds or thousands of machines often took weeks. My background in both machine learning and operating systems convinced me this didn't have to be a manual process, so I built Palisade to automatically detect and remediate these vulnerabilities at the kernel level across an entire fleet.

**What Palisade does:** Palisade watches your systems at the kernel level—syscalls, eBPF traces, process and memory events, and network packets—and uses AI to find OS vulnerabilities other tools miss, then implement the fix automatically across every endpoint.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/fa8c6d6a-b058-4f44-87d0-5511d038718b)

_The Palisade control plane, live against a real kernel (LSM-BPF). The live feed at the bottom: every row is a real syscall decision._

The vulnerabilities it catches are the ones you can't see from the app or network layer alone:

* Privilege escalation
* Remote code execution
* Memory corruption

Most are caught before an exploit ever happens, and the fix is applied immediately, fleet-wide. The same patch that used to take weeks now lands in minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106995&key=user_uploads/2688178/2f4e756d-1348-44a2-bdce-bb3491925da5)

_The host audit: real findings ranked by severity. The bottom one is the cloud-metadata exposure: the same path behind the Capital One breach. One click on **Apply fix** and it's installed as a kernel rule._

Palisade can already detect and fix real problems:

* CVE-2024-1086: use-after-free in the Linux kernel's netfilter (nf_tables); local privilege escalation to root
* CVE-2025-6019: libblockdev/udisks privilege escalation to full root
* CVE-2025-32463: sudo --chroot local privilege escalation to root

**Who it's for:** Companies running a lot of OS-level endpoints, where a single kernel vulnerability multiplies across the whole fleet. Whether it’s network servers or GPUs, we have you covered.

<https://youtu.be/CTVhq7jfTPY>

**Our asks:**

* Intros: if you run a large fleet of OS-level endpoints, or know a security/infra lead who does, I'd love an intro.
* See the demo and tell me if you’d use it. Brutal feedback welcome.

— [prince@palisade-ai.com](mailto:prince@palisade-ai.com), <https://calendly.com/prince-palisade-ai/30min>, DMs welcome

launches.tagline: Your user verifies their identity once, and we return their medical records through one API.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Hubble gives your product a patient's medical records through a single API. Your user verifies their identity once, and we assemble their records from across the providers they've seen and return them for your AI agent to use. Where APIs are not sufficient, we keep going with AI (browser and voice agents). Every request runs on the patient's individual right of access.

**The problem**\
If you're building something that needs a patient's records, there's no clean way to get them. A patient's history is scattered across every provider they've ever seen, and each system is its own island. Most APIs returns the patient-portal subset rather than the full record, and coverage is inconsistent because every health system sets up its integration differently. So most teams either build per-provider integrations for months, fall back to faxes and manual portal logins, or push the problem back onto the patient by asking them to track down their own records or remember a login they set up years ago and have long since lost.

**What Hubble does**\
Your user verifies their identity once, and we go get their records so you don't have to.

* **One verification, no work on your end.** The patient verifies their identity in a couple clicks. After that, assembling the records is our job, not yours and not theirs.
* **We don't stop at the portal subset.** We connect into EHRs and HIEs where they work, and when an API comes back empty we keep going.

launches.body:
After a decade building and scaling companies — including Branch, which[ Govind](https://www.linkedin.com/in/govindkavaturi/) and I grew from zero to $100M+ ARR — we kept hitting the same wall: doing more always meant hiring more. Now, for the first time, it doesn't have to. That's why we built[ **Dock**](https://trydock.ai/).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JO0dwm_NU_s>

AI agents have changed what's possible, which is why we're building again. Dock gives you a team of proactive AI agents  that work alongside you — they talk to each other, hand off work, and take initiative instead of waiting to be prompted. So you steer instead of babysitting a dozen chat windows.

## **The Problem**

AI agents can finally do real work. But today they work alone — isolated chats that sit there waiting for you to prompt them. The moment you run more than one, _you_ become the middleman: copy-pasting context between a dozen windows and unblocking every agent by hand. The more agents you add, the more work you create for yourself. It doesn't scale.

## **The Solution**

Dock turns those isolated agents into a real team. Here's how it works:

### **1. Spin up a team of specialized AI agents in minutes.**

Each agent has a real role, its own objectives, and persistent memory — so it gets better at its job over time instead of resetting every session.

### **2. They work together, proactively.**

Your agents  pursue goals on their own, message each other, and hand off work when one needs something from another — no copy-pasting, no you relaying context. They only come back to you when there's a real decision to make.

### **3. You and your team work right alongside them.**

Everyone — humans and AI agents  — works in the same shared workspace, toward the same goals. The earlier you plug Dock in, the more your agents  learn about how your company actually works.

## **Why this works**

Multi-agent coordination is an infrastructure problem, and we built that infrastructure. Dock runs its own agent harness and runtime, executes in the cloud or on your machine, and gives every agent memory, schedules, and a shared workspace as primitives. Agents working as a team is not a feature we added. It’s what the system is.

## **Why we're building this**

We've spent our careers inside growing companies — hiring, scaling, managing — and felt the coordination drag of every new person you add. When AI made it possible to grow output without growing the team, this problem was already ours. In a real way, Dock found us more than we found it. Today we run our entire company on Dock, and we think soon every company will run on humans and AI agents  working together.

Get early access:[ **trydock.ai**](http://trydock.ai)

launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋, we're Jonathan and Guy, founders of OneCLI.**\
\
🏆 TL;DR**

OneCLI is an open source agent harness for teams. Each employee gets their own sandboxed pro assistant agent, connected to their GitHub, Gmail, Notion, Dropbox, or CRM right from the chat/Slack, while the whole workspace runs under one policy your admins control. \
\
Agents never hold real secrets: the credential is injected at the network layer, per request, after the call is authorized. You can't steal what isn't there.

**Launch Video**\
<https://youtu.be/LUAMdqbl_Rw>

🚧 **The Problem**

Lately, autonomous agents have arrived and shown up everywhere. Tools like OpenClaw and Hermes have become extremely popular and been adopted by open source communities, mostly by individuals. Companies, however, have been left behind: they need integration with their identity providers to enable easy provisioning of agents on behalf of an employee's identity, with least-privilege access.

Those tools have fundamental flaws. Security fundamentals, like secret handling and organization-level control, are missing by default. So companies must choose between weak agents or making them powerful but risky.

✅ **What OneCLI Does**

OneCLI gives teams the whole harness, open source and self-hosted, so agents can be powerful and safe at once:

* **Sandboxed agent per employee:** each agent runs isolated with its own memory, skills, and permissions.
* **Secrets injected at the network layer:** the agent gets a placeholder, the gateway swaps in the real credential per request, after the call is authorized. Credentials never enter the agent's context, memory, or logs.
* **Policy enforced outside the model:** admins define org-wide policy. Block endpoints and scope access per agent.
* **Human-in-the-loop where it counts:** sensitive actions (send the email, delete the Linear ticket, empty the S3 bucket) wait for deterministic approval in the chat.
* **Full identity trail:** every agent is bound to an employee, every call logged with who it acted for and which policy allowed it.

🚀 **Team**

We've spent our careers in security. Jonathan built zero trust network access at Axis Security (acquired by HPE). The core ZTNA idea is that you never trust the client and enforce access outside it, at the network layer. Guy was the first employee at Argon (AppSec company acquired by Aqua Security), protecting client codebases. Agents need exactly the treatment ZTNA gives humans, so we built it.

🙏 **Our Ask**

* Do you want to provide each of your employees with a secure OpenClaw isolated in a sandbox? Shoot me an email: [jonathan@onecli.sh](mailto:jonathan@onecli.sh)
* Star/try the repo:[ https://github.com/onecli/onecli](https://github.com/onecli/onecli). Self-host in minutes, free.

launches.tagline: Agents hold placeholder tokens, real secrets get injected at the network layer
launches.body:
# **🏆 TL;DR**

[**OneCLI**](http://onecli.sh) is an open-source credential gateway for **AI agents**.\
When an agent makes a call, OneCLI swaps in the real credential at the network layer and forwards it. The agent never touches the secret, **you can't steal what isn't there**.\
320K+ downloads, 2,500+ GitHub stars, and the default credential layer in NanoClaw (30K+ stars).

**Ask:** If your team runs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) or autonomous agents in production. And if you can intro us to Head of DevOps or heads of DevSecOps at companies rolling out AI agents, email us at [jonathan@onecli.sh](mailto:jonathan@onecli.sh) \
\
**Sign up for free:** <https://onecli.sh>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106907&key=user_uploads/406823/5294ff50-4b88-4ee7-9c9c-3c776b5b45b5)

<https://youtu.be/5e5pbPEzZfY>

# The Problem

AI agents are doing real work now, which means they need real credentials: API keys, database passwords, OAuth tokens. And there's no safe way to hand them over.

Today, every team does one of two things: hardcode secrets into **.env files** the agent can read, or build a one-off proxy hack. Both mean the **agent holds the secret**. An agent that holds a secret can leak it, through prompt injection, a malicious MCP server, a compromised dependency, or simply by pasting it into a log or a commit.

Secrets management was designed for humans and **deterministic software**. Autonomous agents that read untrusted webpages, install packages, and write their own code are a fundamentally different threat model. The blast radius of one leaked production key is enormous, and teams are granting agents more access every week.

# Our Solution

OneCLI moves the credential out of the agent entirely.

You run one command, and every outbound call from your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline) or autonomous agent (OpenClaw, Hermes, NanoClaw) routes through OneCLI. The agent only ever sees placeholder tokens. On each request, the proxy:

1. Matches the request by host/path
2. Checks it against policy
3. Swaps the placeholder for the real credential
4. Forwards the request

The agent never holds the secret, so there's nothing to steal, log, or exfiltrate. \
Secrets are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest. The whole thing runs in a single Docker container with no external dependencies. It works with anything that can set HTTPS_PROXY.

For teams, we already support integration with IdPs and organization-wide policy setup, giving you full control and visibility over every access made by your agents.

# Why this and not the PAM/identity vendors?

Because the credential problem for agents is a **network problem, not an identity problem**. Vault-based tools (1Password, HashiCorp Vault) still hand the secret to the agent to authenticate. The agent holds it, so the agent can leak it. OneCLI injects the credential at the wire: transparent injection, policy enforced on every outbound request, and the secret never enters the agent's context in the first place.

# The Team

We've spent our careers in security. Guy (CTO) was the first hire at Argon (acquired by Aqua Security). Jonathan (CEO) worked on ZTNA and network security at Axis Security (acquired by HPE), after serving in Israeli Military Intelligence.

We hit this problem ourselves. Before OneCLI we built ChartDB together, an open-source database tool with 20K+ GitHub stars, and while building an agent orchestration layer on top of it, we kept hitting the same wall: there was no safe way to hand an autonomous agent credentials. Every team we talked to was either hardcoding API keys or duct-taping proxies. So we built the thing we wished existed.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106907&key=user_uploads/406823/ff451063-51d2-4c13-9c5f-cd1863b8c648)

# The Ask

If you know a Head of DevOps or DevSecOps lead at a company rolling out AI agents, we'd love an intro.

[jonathan@onecli.sh](mailto:jonathan@onecli.sh)

launches.title: Edviro - AI that operates energy infrastructure
launches.tagline: AI to operate energy infrastructure
launches.body:
# **Edviro: AI that operates energy infrastructure**

Hi all,

We’re Hursh and Tanuj, founders of Edviro.

**TL;DR:** Edviro connects to a facility’s BMS, utility, sensor, equipment, and maintenance systems to build a world model of how the facility behaves. We use that model to detect problems, simulate interventions before anything is changed, and coordinate the best next action. We’re live in **34 facilities**, have identified more than **$400K in avoidable energy costs**, and are now opening our first partnerships with data center operators.\
\
<https://youtu.be/0sTQlaQGlOY>

## **The problem**

Data centers are expected to drive roughly half of U.S. electricity-demand growth through 2030.

This is usually framed as a problem of producing more electricity. That is only part of it.

Power must be delivered to the right sites, on the timelines data centers are being built, with the reliability their workloads require. Once a facility has that power, its operators still need to extract as much useful compute as possible from every available megawatt without compromising uptime.

Inside a data center, power, cooling, controls, equipment, workloads, and maintenance are tightly coupled. A workload shift changes the thermal profile. A cooling-control change affects both energy use and equipment margins. A maintenance decision can alter redundancy and available capacity.

Yet the data and workflows used to manage these systems remain fragmented across BMS, DCIM, EPMS, meters, sensors, maintenance software, vendor portals, and spreadsheets.

Most existing systems can display telemetry or raise an alarm. They cannot reliably model how the entire facility will respond before an operator changes a setpoint, shifts a workload, services equipment, or adds capacity.

Operators are left making high-stakes decisions with incomplete system-level context.

## **What Edviro does**

Edviro turns a facility’s operational data into a continuously updated world model.

By “world model,” we mean a model that estimates the current state of the physical system, learns how its components interact, and predicts how it will respond to a proposed action. 

Edviro:

* Integrates data from building controls, utilities, sensors, equipment, and maintenance systems
* Detects anomalies, energy waste, equipment degradation, and capacity constraints
* Simulates operational and maintenance interventions before they are deployed
* Recommends the best action while accounting for cost, reliability, and physical constraints
* Uses agents to coordinate approvals, work orders, investigations, and follow-through
* Verifies whether the expected operational and energy impact actually occurred

For a data center, this could mean determining whether existing power and cooling infrastructure can support additional IT load, testing a control-sequence change before deploying it, identifying which equipment issue is constraining capacity, or prioritizing maintenance based on the capacity and reliability it would recover.

We initially keep operators in control of every consequential action. As the models are validated and earn trust, more of the operating loop can be automated.

## **Why we started with schools**

Edviro began when I was 17 and working with my high school’s facilities team. I was given a year of district utility bills to analyze, built software to parse them, and discovered roughly **$360,000 in gas overbilling**.

We found that this was not an isolated problem. Schools operate large portfolios of aging, mixed-vendor infrastructure with fragmented controls, incomplete data, lean facilities teams, and very little room for wasted budget.

They forced us to build for the messy reality of physical infrastructure rather than clean laboratory data.

Today, Edviro is live in **34 facilities** and has identified more than **$400,000 in avoidable energy costs** for building operators.

A school is obviously not a data center. Data centers have denser instrumentation, much tighter uptime requirements, and more complex coupling between power, cooling, and compute. 

What transfers is the underlying architecture: connecting heterogeneous operational systems, estimating the state of a physical facility, simulating interventions, coordinating action across teams, and verifying the result. We are now building the data-center-specific models, integrations, and safety constraints directly with operators. Our first relevant research benchmark can be found here: <https://x.com/hursheybar2/status/2083299315003593037?s=20>

## **Where we’re going**

The current generation of facilities software tells operators what has already happened.

We want Edviro to understand what is happening now, predict what will happen next, and help execute the safest and highest-value response.

As electricity becomes one of the primary constraints on AI growth, building more infrastructure will not be enough. We also need to operate the infrastructure we already have far more intelligently.

The long-term goal is not another dashboard. It is infrastructure that can understand itself and increasingly operate itself.

## **Asks**

1. **We’re looking for data center operators to become early design partners.** We are especially interested in facilities dealing with power or cooling constraints, capacity-expansion planning, recurring manual investigations, fragmented controls, or reactive maintenance. We can begin read-only, with operators retaining approval over every action.
2. **We’re hiring energy-modeling engineers** across thermal systems, power systems, controls, scientific machine learning, and physical simulation.

If you operate a data center—or know the team responsible for operating one—we’d love to talk.

[**www.edviro.com**](http://www.edviro.com)

Hi all 👋, We’re Michael and Charles, founders of Conifer.

**TLDR:** Conifer is one interface for both local and cloud models, available today as **Juniper**, our consumer-facing app. It routes each request to the most cost-effective option, beginning with your own hardware. Most requests are processed locally without API fees, reducing paid token volume by up to 80%.

**📺 Launch Video:**[ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QLVNISmtet0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QLVNISmtet0)

**❓ The problem**: Model labs direct every request to the cloud, with no incentive to route your queries to a cheaper competitor or a free, on-device model. That may benefit them, but it’s unnecessarily costly for you. Whether it’s a simple typo fix or a complex architecture problem, the request is sent to a data center, exposing your data to third parties and increasing your monthly spend. This quickly adds up for teams running coding agents, customer support, and other high-volume workloads. When handling financials, patient records, or customer data, teams must also trust that a cloud provider’s security is as robust as promised.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105897&key=user_uploads/3664042/6dbc9654-b4df-453d-a02e-3ea71302316d)

**🔨 What Conifer does:** Conifer routes every request from the bottom up:

Tier 0: Your own hardware, with $0 in API fees

Tier 1: An efficient cloud model

Tier 2: A frontier model for the most demanding queries

The majority of requests are processed locally, ensuring that cloud pricing applies only when actually necessary, drastically reducing paid token volume. Additionally, Conifer consolidates disparate subscriptions, dashboards, and API keys within a single unified interface.

For sensitive workloads 🕵️, **local-only mode** disables cloud routing entirely, so all conversations and data remain completely on-device.

🏃‍♂️ **Ensuring the local tier is fast enough:** This routing only works if the local tier is reliable, so we built Conifer's inference engine from the ground up in Rust. On Apple Silicon, decode speeds reach up to 60% faster than llama.cpp.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=105897&key=user_uploads/3664042/79b464dc-667b-48af-a1ba-5cdd089b1dc8)

On-device operation with Conifer is now the default starting point for inference, rather than a feature limited to hobbyist use.

**Asks:**

1. Try Juniper with a one-click download @[ conifer.build](http://conifer.build), or reach out to us at [contact@conifer.build](mailto:contact@conifer.build) to have a model running in under two minutes.
2. Introduce us to teams with high monthly token spend. If teams are incurring significant API costs and want to optimize unit economics without rebuilding their stack, we would like to connect.

Hey everyone. You’ve might of heard of Open AI, Open Router, OpenCode, OpenWork….

When a better model ships, your coworker gets better the same day, benefiting from the performance and cost improvements.

OpenTag is an AI coworker that lives inside of Slack. You invite it into the channels you want. It picks up how the company runs, how decisions are made, who owns what. It asks for tools and visibility the way an A-player hire does, and it tries to grow its own scope and agency. It starts as an intern and tries to earn the COO job. launches.body:
Hey everyone! 👋 \
\
We're Macy, Faiz and Niyaz - co-founders of[ Papaya](https://papaya.fyi) 

**TL;DR**

Papaya is the optimization engine for AI agents. Connect your production agent and Papaya watches every action, finds what's hurting quality, cost, and latency, and gives you the fix. Once a fix is in place, Papaya makes sure your agent doesn't regress. Teams running Papaya are seeing 20%+ improvements to quality, latency, and cost.

**Ask:** If you run an agent in production, connect it to Papaya. Grab a time to get started [here](https://cal.com/macy-mody/macy-papaya).

<https://youtu.be/cG9iIVB5Psk>

**The Problem**

We’ve been building agentic systems for years (6 years to be exact…before it was cool), including really large ones that helped run major workflows inside Amazon. We know firsthand that the hard part isn’t getting an agent to work, it’s keeping it working at a high quality bar. We consistently saw that every model update and every prompt change shifted behavior in ways nobody caught until something downstream looked wrong. The only way to find out what changed was to pull traces and read them by hand.

Most companies shipping agents today are focused on the next feature for customers and they don't have time to fully maintain what's already been released. When we built our own agent as a three-person team, we hit the same wall. We needed to make sure our agent had high quality answers, was fast for our customers, and as low cost as possible, but we had to look at everything by hand. Every hour we spent examining traces was an hour we couldn’t spend on new product development. That's why we built Papaya.

**How Papaya works 🔧** 

At Papaya, our goal is to do the hard AI engineering work for you, staying up to date on the latest and greatest research so you can take advantage of this knowledge through optimizations. Simply stream your production traces through a lightweight SDK. From there, Papaya:

* **Finds your use cases**: groups every run by the job the agent is doing, so you're looking at "refund requests," not "run 4812."
* **Runs 200+ analyses**: checks every use case against 200+ research-backed failure patterns across quality, cost, and latency.
* **Ranks the fixes by impact**: every recommendation comes with an estimated effect on quality, latency, and cost. Approve the ones you want directly in Papaya and Papaya opens the PR.
* **Watches for regression**: once a fix ships, Papaya keeps checking that the improvement holds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=115486&key=user_uploads/2135001/0a49f356-ac11-44d5-bcc1-69caf4ba64d9)


**Our Ask 🙏**

* Run an agent in production? Connect it to Papaya. Grab a time with us [here](https://cal.com/macy-mody/macy-papaya).
* Know any companies spending tons of time maintaining and fixing their agents? Intro us at [macy@papaya.fyi](mailto:macy@papaya.fyi).
* Building agents and want a second set of eyes? Ping us. We are happy to help however we can!

**The Team**

We've spent over 10 years building large scale agentic systems at Amazon, and we've scaled other YC startups from $0 to $10M ARR through acquisition. We started out building an analytics agent. The harness we built to optimize our own agent became the center of every prospect conversation, so we pivoted to it. Meet our team below :)

launches.title: DeepMark - Reinventing Trust in Voice
launches.tagline: A live watermark inside AI voice that survives phone calls
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/76SqazbxK4w>

Hey, we are Slavko and Kosta 👋

We have been working together for six years, first as two researchers at the University of Montenegro, now as founders. Somewhere along the way, we became best friends. Kosta is our CSO, and I am the CEO.

**The problem**

Voice is uniquely vulnerable to impersonation. A few seconds of audio is enough to clone anyone, and the same voice agents that answer a bank's phone can be turned around and pointed at the bank's customers. People have started to hesitate before picking up. Good technology scales good outcomes, and it scales bad ones just as well. Our job is simple. Restore trust in voice.

**What we built**

DeepMark is real-time audio watermarking for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we put a certificate inside the sound itself, on the voice company's side, as the voice is being generated. Not metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The certificate becomes part of the voice.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/b3239118-82c1-4fb4-82c2-f4363685a0be)

Then the voice goes out into the real world, and the real world is rough on audio. Compression, codecs, a bad connection, a cheap speaker, a worse microphone. Think about how flat a human voice sounds over the phone. Our certificate survives the trip. On the other end, a phone, a call center, or an API reads it and shows who is speaking, who issued the certificate, and whether this agent is allowed to be on the line. Detectors ask whether audio is fake. We answer who is authorized to speak.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/171abdf5-efb9-442b-a153-dbbb1ba981d4)

**Why this is hard**

Four things have to hold at the same time. It has to be real time, or a phone call makes no sense, and voice companies already fight for every millisecond. It has to leave the audio quality alone, nobody trades a worse voice for a safer one. It has to survive the phone line. And the ID has to be long enough, because the longer the ID, the more certificates we can issue. A watermark that works beautifully in the lab falls apart the moment audio meets a phone line. And a live call has no file to sign. Nothing survives the trip except the sound itself, so the identity has to live inside the sound. We spent years hitting that wall. Then we built a tool that measures all four at once and published it, so anyone can check our work, and everyone else's.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/a9930538-1deb-4609-8938-4bdbcf8c88ce)

**How we got here**

Our mentor, who did his PhD in digital watermarking, told us not to bother. The field was saturated, nothing left to contribute. We were too stubborn to listen, and our learning-based approach turned out to be one of the first of its kind.

Kosta wrote his PhD on watermarking along the way. I am still writing mine! We published some of the earliest work in deep audio watermarking, cited by teams at Meta, Microsoft, Sony, and Adobe. This year our robustness benchmark landed in IEEE Access, and our AWARE paper was accepted at EUSIPCO. Before YC, we signed our first platform license with a leading voice AI provider, and it is now in production.

**Our ask**

We want to meet voice AI companies. If you build voice models, book 20 minutes with us and we will run DeepMark on your own audio, so you can see the mark survive your calls. The EU AI Act's marking rules already apply and the 2 December deadline for systems on the market is close, so this is a good month to talk. If you know someone at a voice AI platform, an intro means a lot to us.

[slavko@deepmark.me](mailto:slavko@deepmark.me), or book a demo at [deepmark.me](http://deepmark.me). Thanks for reading. 🇲🇪 → 🌉
